posts.post_title: Documenting Your Burn Injuries: Steps to Take After an Accident
posts.before:
If you have been injured in a burn accident, you may be wondering if you can sue for compensation. This article will explore the topic of burn injury cases and provide some valuable insights into what you can expect.

Types of Burn Injuries

Burn injuries are classified into four categories, depending on the severity of the burn. 

  • First-degree burns are the mildest, affecting only the outer layer of skin.
  • Second-degree burns penetrate deeper into the skin, causing blisters and pain.
  • Third-degree burns are even more severe, damaging all layers of skin and possibly requiring skin grafts.
  • Fourth-degree burns are the most severe, potentially causing damage to the bone and tendons.

Steps to Take After a Burn Injury

If you have suffered a burn injury due to someone else's negligence or carelessness, you may be entitled to compensation. However, it's essential to take the correct steps to protect your health and potential legal claim. 

  1. Seek Medical Attention

You may require immediate medical assistance to minimize the long-term impact of your burn injury. However, no matter how severe your injury, you should err on the side of caution and be seen by doctors. This is the only way to help ensure your health issues are being dealt with the right way. Seeking medical attention right away can also help link the accident and your injury.

  1. Document Your Injuries

Injuries will change over time, especially burn injuries. If your case goes to trial, it may be months or years before a judge or jury evaluates the evidence. Your injuries may have healed during that time. For this reason, it is important to document your injuries.

Take pictures of your injuries as they progress and document each stage of healing. This will help the judge or jury get a better idea of your injuries and their severity. Your lawyer may also recommend that you keep a pain journal so that you keep track of how you were feeling while you were undergoing medical treatment and recovery.

  1. Contact A Lawyer 

A qualified burn lawyer can examine the specific circumstances surrounding your claim and determine the identity of potential defendants who intentionally or negligently contributed to your injuries. They can also investigate how the at-fault individual's actions led to serious burn injuries and handle communication with him or her or the insurance company.

Compensation for Burn Injuries

It's important to note that compensation for burn injuries can vary widely, depending on the type of damages you have suffered. A burn injury lawsuit may demand damages for the following:

  • Scarring
  • Disfigurement
  • Tissue Damage
  • Infection
  • Organ Failure
  • Circulation Problems
  • Failure of the Senses
  • Loss of Sensation
  • Respiratory Problems
  • Permanent Disability
  • Pain and Suffering

An experienced burn injury lawyer can examine the facts of your case to determine the potential compensation you may be able to receive from your burn injury claim, including the fair value of each form of compensation.

Examples of Successful Burn Injury Cases

The most famous example of a successful burn injury case is the McDonald's hot coffee case, where a woman was scalded by hot coffee that was served to her by an employee. She spilled the coffee on herself, which led to third-degree burns and the need to get skin grafts on her inner thighs and elsewhere. The company continued to serve the coffee at high temperatures despite being aware of several other reports of their coffee causing injuries. The jury found the company liable, and the woman was awarded millions in compensation.

Other situations where burn injury victims may be more likely to receive compensation include:

  • Employers who had employees work around dangerous chemicals without proper safety equipment
  • Individuals who intentionally started fires and injured people on the property
  • Motorists who caused accidents that led to thermal burns
  • Healthcare providers who caused radiation burns through the misuse of X-rays or radiation therapy
  • Manufacturers who negligently caused harm to consumers because of toxic ingredients.

Roden Law - Your Personal Injury Attorneys

If you or a loved one has been suffering from a burn injury due to the negligent actions of another, the Charleston burn injury lawyers at Roden Law can help. We will investigate your claim to determine who should be held accountable for the damages that you have suffered. Contact us today for a free consultation to determine if you have a viable claim.

posts.post_title: How to Avoid Bicycle Accidents
posts.before:
A new report from the AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety reveals that hit-and-run car crash deaths are on the rise, and almost 70 percent of the victims are pedestrians or those riding bicycles. The increase in deaths is partly caused by an increase in people riding their bicycles to work or as a form of exercise. If you were injured or lost a loved one in a bicycle accident, our Charleston personal injury lawyers may be able to help you pursue compensation. We offer a free, no obligation legal consultation and do not charge for representing you unless you receive fair compensation.

Reducing the Risk of a Bicycle Crash

Fortunately, there are many ways that cyclists can reduce the risk of being injured in a bicycle crash, including:

Being Careful at Intersections

Intersections are some of the most dangerous locations for cyclists, which is why you need to be extremely careful when approaching these areas and riding through them. Slow down when approaching an intersection and look carefully for approaching traffic. Even if you have the right of way, check that no other vehicles are coming. Carefully monitor traffic signs and signals – if a light is about to change, you might be better waiting to go through the intersection.  As you go through the intersection, watch for any approaching cars. You want as much time as possible to maneuver to avoid a collision if a car is coming at you.

Increasing Visibility

Bicyclists take up less space and are less noticeable than other vehicles. For these reasons, it is important that cyclists take care to increase their visibility. There are several ways to accomplish this, including:
  • Wearing light-colored or luminescent clothing day and night when cycling
  • Adding reflective tape to clothing
  • Using a rear reflector on your bike
  • Avoiding blind spots
  • Avoiding emerging from a covered area without stopping or looking for dangers ahead
  • Avoiding riding on a narrow rural road when it is dark outside

Signaling Properly

Signaling properly allows other motorists to know your intentions. The following signals should be used:
  • Left-hand turn – Signal by extending your left arm to the side and keeping it level with the left side of your bike.
  • Right-hand turn – Extend your right arm and hand, keeping it level with the rest of your body.

Avoiding Parked Cars

Many drivers do not look for approaching bike riders before opening their car doors after parking. This often results in bicyclists crashing into open car doors, particularly when cars are parallel parked. You can reduce your risk of this type of accident by putting at least four feet between your bike and any parked cars. You should also check parked cars for drivers or passengers so you will be prepared in case one of them opens a door. The more time you have to react, the more likely you are to avoid an accident.

Wearing a Helmet

While wearing a helmet will not prevent an accident from happening, it can help minimize any damage an accident causes and potentially save your life. Some guidelines for bike helmets include:
  • The helmet and straps should fit snugly on your head.
  • The helmet should be level.
  • Use a brightly-colored helmet with reflective tape to increase visibility.

Sometimes no matter how safe you are, others may cause you to suffer injury in a bicycle accident. Contacting an experienced personal injury lawyer can help you protect your claim. At Roden Law, our team of legal professionals can help you seek compensation for the many costs involved in an accident, such as medical expenses, lost wages, and other damages. If you were injured in a bike accident, we can explain your rights during a free initial consultation. Since we only collect attorney’s fees if we help you recover compensation, you have nothing to lose by scheduling a free, no-obligation consultation to discuss your rights.

posts.post_title: Who Can Be Liable an Auto Accident Caused by Poor Road Conditions?
posts.before:
Although many auto collisions are attributed to driver negligence, poor road conditions are also a common contributing factor to many car accidents. When this occurs, there may be several parties at fault for your accident, including local, state and federal government agencies. The Charleston auto accident attorneys at Roden Law have handled numerous car accident claims and know how to identify which parties can be held liable for the damages you suffered. Contact us to schedule a free, no obligation consultation as soon as possible after an accident. We will review your claim to determine if you may be entitled to compensation for your medical expenses, lost wages and pain and suffering. Below, our Charleston personal injury lawyers review several factors that may help us determine which party is liable for a car accident caused by hazardous roadway conditions.

Common Roadway Hazards

In Georgia, there are several types of dangerous conditions that create hazard for drivers. Although some hazards may seem common, they still increase the likelihood of causing a serious car accident. These roadway hazards may include:

Potholes

When a vehicle runs into a pothole, it can cause serious damage to a vehicle and may even result in an accident. Potholes are the result of expanding and contracting groundwater below the pavement. As this occurs, the roadway will start to give way, and the size of the pothole will continue to increase as cars run over it if not fixed.

Poor Roadway Maintenance

Failing to properly maintain roadways can lead to several hazards that increase the risk of an auto accident, including:
  • Uneven pavement
  • Erosion
  • Faded lane markings
  • Broken guardrails
  • Missing traffic signs

Dangerous Roadway Design

Even with proper construction, poor design of a roadway can put motorists in danger. Flaws in roadway design can cause dangerous conditions that increase the risk of an accident, such as:
  • Curves that are too sharp
  • Merging lanes or on-ramps that are too short
  • Poor lighting
  • Inadequate warnings of dangerous conditions

Who is Responsible for Maintaining the Roadway?

In Georgia, cities, counties and state government agencies are responsible for maintaining roadways and ensuring any known hazard is fixed. There are several factors that may determine which entity is responsible for fixing the hazard, such as the location of the roadway and type of hazard. However, there may be instances where multiple agencies are liable for the same roadway. For example, the state may be responsible for filling a pothole while the county or city is responsible for clearing the roadway of debris. When a hazardous condition causes an accident, you must prove the responsible government entity neglected to maintain the roadway. This requires you to prove the at-fault entity failed to uphold its obligation to clear any known hazard, or adequately warn motorists of its existence. Additionally, if a dangerous roadway hazard long enough for the liable entity to know of its existence, but failed to become aware of the hazard, the government entity may still be held liable for any resulting damages.

Can I Sue a Government Agency in Georgia?

If you are injured in an auto accident that resulted from a government entity’s negligence, you may be able to file a personal injury claim against the at-fault entity. However, filing a personal injury claim against a government entity in Georgia is very different than bringing legal action against a person or corporation. This includes providing a written claim to the government entity responsible for causing the accident. Your claim should include the:
  • Time and place of the accident
  • Extent of your injury
  • Amount of damages you intend to pursue
  • Negligent action that caused your injury
Additionally, Georgia imposes a different time line for accident victims who are filing a personal injury claim against the government. If you are filing a claim against a city or municipal county, you have six months to provide notice about your claim. Likewise, if you are filing a claim against the state, you must present notice of your claim within 12 months of the accident. If you do not follow these strict deadlines, your claim will likely be dismissed and you cannot obtain compensation for your injury.

Contact an Attorney for Help

If you were injured in a car accident caused by poor road conditions, you may be entitled to compensation for your medical bills, lost wages, and pain and suffering. The Savannah car accident lawyers of Roden Law will evaluate your case and help you pursue the compensation you deserve. Schedule a free, no obligation consultation today and learn which legal options may be available for pursuing compensation for your injuries. We only work on a contingency fee basis, which means there are no upfront fees and you only have to pay us if we recover compensation for your claim.

posts.post_title: Filing a Claim for an Accident Caused by a Teen Driver
posts.before:
There are about 13.2 million teen drivers on the road every day, according to data from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). What happens when one of those teens is responsible for a motor vehicle accident resulting in injuries to you or a loved one? Call a Charleston car accident lawyer if you were involved in an accident with a teen driver to learn about your potential legal options. Below, we discuss some of the ways the teenage driver or his or her parent may be held liable for your damages.

Parental Liability

Almost every single state has parental liability laws in case their child causes death, injuries, property damage through negligent or willful acts that bring harm to others. Parents and any legal guardians who have custody of a minor may be held financially responsible for damages caused by the minor, including damages from a car accident. If a teen driver is responsible for the accident that caused your injuries, you may have legal recourse to pursue compensation from the teen’s parents. This usually means filing a claim against the parent or legal guardian’s car insurance policy. Teenagers usually cannot afford car insurance, which is why they are often on their parents’ plans. However, most insurance companies require that anyone residing in the same household who has a license is listed under the homeowner’s motor vehicle insurance policy. It is important to note that car insurance typically follows the car. Even if the teenager was not listed on the policy, if the car is owned and insured by the parent, the parent’s liability insurance likely applies.

What if the Teenager was Driving a Car Not Owned by His or Her Parents?

This could be a much more complicated situation. For example, maybe the teenager was driving a car loaned to the parents by someone else. If the teenager had permission to drive the car, the insurance on the car likely applies. However, if the teenager did not have permission, such as if the teenager’s parents told him or her not to drive the car, liability insurance on the car may not apply.

What About Willful or Malicious Actions?

It is important to note insurance policies often have exclusions for willful or malicious actions. If the teenager’s actions were intentional, insurance on the car may not apply. In these situations, it may be necessary to file a lawsuit.

Tips to Help Keep Your Own Teen Driver Safe

According to an NHTSA study, about 33 percent of high school students nationwide admitted to texting and driving while 12 percent of distracted drivers involved in fatal car accidents were teens aged 15 to 19. Statistics like these may have a sobering effect on parents who have children on the verge of getting a driver’s license. These statistics also highlight how important it is to discuss road safety with your teen as early as possible. There are also some practical things you can do to help keep your teen driver safe:
  • Talk to them about the dangers of distracted driving
  • Show them data about teen drivers in the U.S.
  • Lead by example and be a safe driver

Let Us Help. Call Today

Teen drivers cause thousands of accidents resulting in all sorts of injuries. If you or a loved one were injured due to a teenager’s negligent driving, you may be eligible to seek compensation from the liability insurance under the parent’s car insurance policy. Let our attorneys at Roden Law help you through this complicated process while you focus on recovering from your injuries. We have successfully recovered millions in compensation for injury victims since 2013. If you choose to hire us, the consultation is free, and you do not owe us anything unless we recover compensation on your behalf.

posts.post_title: Can a Police Report Help Prove Liability After an Accident?
posts.before:
No matter the severity of an accident, if you plan on filing an insurance claim, you should contact law enforcement to investigate and file a police report. This report often serves as an important piece of evidence as your attorney works to validate your claim. Below, our Charleston car accident lawyers discuss the value of a police report in proving liability in an injury claim. We also explain how we may be able to help you through the claims process without any out-of-pocket costs to you.

Establishing an Objective Third-Party Narrative

When law enforcement officers arrive at an accident scene, their objective is not just to ensure the safety of those involved and the safe flow of traffic. They also need to complete a report that will serve as an objective third-party observation of what may have caused the crash. Police officers usually note several factors that may have contributed to an accident, including the following:
  • Weather conditions
  • Visibility conditions
  • Roadway conditions
  • Driver impairment
  • Speeding
The police report may also note how a driver may have acted negligently before an accident occurred and who may be to blame for the crash.

Witness Statements

When an accident only causes minor damage, injury victims may be able to collect witness information on their own while police conduct their investigation into the crash. But what happens when an accident results in serious injuries that render you or your passengers unconscious, which makes it impossible to collect witness statements? Fortunately, law enforcement officers can also collect witness statements and document them in the police report. Sometimes, passing drivers who witness an accident may call 9-1-1, but they do not stay at the scene. A police report may provide a statement from a passing driver, which you may not have been able to obtain on your own. For example, a passerby who witnesses a hit-and-run crash may call the police to report it. He or she may have a description of the vehicle and a license plate number. You may not have been able to obtain this information because of poor lighting, obstructions on the road or the fact you were seriously injured in the crash and rendered unconscious.

Traffic Citations

Police reports usually note which driver was issued a citation for a traffic violation, such as:
  • Speeding
  • Running a red light
  • Improperly passing
  • Following too closely
  • Texting and driving
  • And more
If the other driver involved in your accident gets a ticket, it may be a powerful piece of evidence to help prove liability.

Damage

The police report also describes damage to the vehicles involved in the accident. Sometimes this can help to prove liability for the crash. posts.post_title: How Do I Pay My Medical Bills While My Personal Injury Claim is Open?
posts.before:
If you are injured in an accident caused by someone else’s negligence, you may be eligible for compensation. However, the process of filing a claim and recovering the compensation you need for medical bills and other damages takes time. How do you pay for the medical treatment you need while your lawyer seeks a settlement? You can discuss your options for paying for medical care while your injury claim is being processed with a licensed car accident attorney in Charleston in a free consultation. We do not charge you anything up front and only get paid if you do.

File a Claim Through Your Own Car Insurance Policy

Unlike some other at-fault states, South Carolina does not offer Personal Injury Protection (PIP) coverage to drivers. PIP pays for the policyholder’s medical treatment. In South Carolina, drivers instead have the option to purchase Medical Payments (MedPay) coverage to help with medical bills while awaiting a verdict or settlement for an injury claim. If you do not have health insurance or are concerned that it will not cover much of your medical costs, you may want to consider purchasing MedPay. Car crash injuries can be very expensive to treat, and many people do not have the financial means to pay for it. Missing payments will likely hurt your credit score and may result in calls from debt collectors, adding more stress to an already stressful situation.

Using Your Health Insurance Policy

If you have health insurance, this may be the best option while you wait for a potential settlement of your claim. This is what often happens, as many drivers do not have MedPay coverage in their car insurance policies. However, the health insurance company is likely to pursue reimbursement from the liable insurance company for any costs they paid out. This process is called subrogation, and it means your compensation award would be reduced by the amount your health insurance paid out. With the help from one of our attorneys, you may be able to negotiate a lower payback amount so you may be able to keep more of the compensation your lawyer recovers.

Negotiate a Payment Agreement with the Medical Provider

If you do not have MedPay or health insurance, our attorneys may be able to work with you to find medical providers who will agree to treat you on a contingency basis. This means that our attorneys would negotiate with the doctor or medical center to have their services paid for after your claim is settled or a verdict is reached in your favor.

Other Options

Every injury victim’s life situation is just as unique as his or her injury claim, which means that some people may have other options to help pay for medical treatment:
  • Medicaid
  • Medicare
  • Veterans Affairs Benefits
Family members or loved ones may also be willing and able to help. You could pay them back after you receive your settlement. Hospitals and other medical providers are often willing to negotiate monthly payment amounts. You may be able to negotiate an amount you can afford to pay until your injury claim is settled. However, it is important to remember if you miss a payment, the provider may demand you immediately pay the rest of the bill. It is important not to delay medical treatment, as it could result in the worsening of your injuries. If you are concerned about how to pay your medical bills, Roden Law may be able to help.

Call Roden Law Today to Discuss Your Claim

Whether you need help filing your injury claim or negotiating a lower rate for your medical bills, our attorneys are prepared to assist you. Do not let the insurance companies take advantage of you. Let the attorneys at Roden Law stand up for your rights. We do not charge you anything while we work on your claim and only get paid if you do.

posts.post_title: Epilepsy & Driving: Liability for Seizure-Related Crashes
posts.before:
Epilepsy affects millions worldwide, including approximately three million individuals in the U.S. Given the potential for seizures and blackouts, it raises an important question: should people with epilepsy be allowed to drive? Moreover, can they be held liable for car accidents caused by seizures? At Roden Law, our dedicated car accident lawyers in Charleston specialize in handling complex cases involving medical conditions or medication. If you've been involved in a seizure-related accident or experienced a seizure while driving, our knowledgeable attorneys can provide a free case evaluation to explain your rights and assess whether you're eligible for compensation.

Dangers of Driving with Epilepsy/Seizures

Driving with epilepsy can pose significant risks, even if you're currently taking medication to control your symptoms. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported in 2015 that less than half of those on medication were seizure-free. An epileptic incident can occur at any time, and in the moments leading up to it and during a seizure, these are some of the symptoms that could impair your ability to drive safely:
  • Seizure-induced confusion
  • Loss of consciousness
  • Uncontrollable body jerking
  • Cognitive impairment
  • Anxiety
  • Staring spells or feeling “spaced out”
  • Headaches
  • Temporary paralysis after a seizure
  • Memory lapses
  • Temporary loss of bowel control

Driver’s License Requirements for Seizures

In many states, individuals with epilepsy can obtain a driver's license if they haven't experienced a seizure within the last six months. Those who have seizures exclusively at night may be eligible for a limited license, permitting daytime driving, even if a seizure occurred within the previous six months. To learn more about the Epilepsy related Driving Laws in your state, click here to learn more.

Reporting Medical Limitations

Doctors may not be obligated to report patients with epilepsy, but they can report anyone with a known condition that impairs their ability to safely operate a vehicle. Additionally, concerned individuals such as relatives, courts, judges, law enforcement officers, or citizens can submit non-anonymous letters to express their concerns. The DMV may then require the individual to undergo a medical evaluation and provide documented proof of their ability to drive safely.

Determining Liability for a Crash Involving Seizures

If a person has a seizure and causes an accident, it doesn't automatically make them legally responsible for the collision. Various factors come into play when determining liability, including the individual's history of epileptic events or seizures, whether they were under the care of a doctor for epilepsy, and whether they had been seizure-free for at least six months. While a seizure's involvement in the accident may attribute some fault to the person with the medical condition, the issue remains complex, particularly if they had no prior diagnosis or seizure history.

How Comparative Fault Comes into Play

Georgia uses a modified comparative negligence system to apportion fault between two or more parties whose negligence contributed to an accident. According to this system, if you were less than 50 percent at fault for the accident, you can still pursue compensation for the damages you sustained. However, your level of recovery will be reduced by your fault percentage. For example, if you are found 10 percent liable for the accident, you can only receive 90 percent of the total value of your damages. If it is determined that you are more than 50 percent at-fault for the accident, you cannot recover any damages.

Call Us Right Now for Help with Your Claim

If you've been injured in an accident caused by someone experiencing a seizure or if you had a seizure while driving, it's essential to seek the help of an attorney experienced in personal injury law. 

The dedicated legal team at Roden Law can review the circumstances surrounding your case and explain your rights to you. We work on a contingency fee basis, so you are charged nothing unless we recover compensation for your accident. Call us today to schedule a confidential and complimentary consultation.

posts.post_title: Loud Music and Crashes: What Charleston Drivers Need to Know
posts.before:
Loud music while driving has become more common due to better car stereos and easy access to music. While enjoyable, it can be dangerous. Playing music at high volumes can affect driving skills and make accidents more likely.

Table of Contents

  • Risks of Driving with Loud Music
  • The Impact of Loud Music in Charleston
  • How to Reduce Car Crash Related to Loud Music
  • How Claims May Be Affected in Loud Music Related Car Crashes?
  • Contact Roden Law Today
If you were involved in a car accident due to loud music, you may be eligible to pursue compensation. Our Charleston car accident lawyers can walk you through your legal rights during a free consultation.

Call today to learn about your potential legal rights. 1-844-RESULTS.

Risks of Driving With Loud Music

Drivers have a legal duty to stay focused on the road. Loud music can become distracting and disrupt a driver's ability to pay attention, which could lead to following types of distractions:

Cognitive Overload

Drivers may experience cognitive overload when the brain is overwhelmed by too many things happening at once. For instance, loud music with complex lyrics could leave drivers with less mental capacity to process important information. A driver could be too busy singing the lyrics to a song and fail to see a traffic light or stop sign, causing them to fail yield the right of way. This could in a crash if another vehicle is already traveling through the intersection.

Auditory Distraction

Auditory distractions are external sounds that prevent drivers from hearing vital cues on the road or highway. Loud music is an auditory distraction that conceals crucial environmental noise around you as you drive. For instance, it can conceal sirens, horns and tire screeches. If drivers cannot hear emergency vehicles approaching, it could lead to a serious crash involving another driver or emergency vehicle.

Attention Shifts

Loud music can cause drivers to shift their attention between listening to music and paying attention to the road. This shift can result in delayed responses to changes in traffic conditions or obstacles. For instance, if a driver is engaging in their music, they may not realize that they must slow down due to traffic congestions. As a result, drivers may not react swiftly to sudden changes, causing them to rear-end a vehicle in front of them.

The Impact of Loud Music in Charleston

Driving in Charleston is already tricky due to its historic cobblestone streets, busy tourist areas and community events. Loud music can present these driving challenges:

Narrow, Historic Streets

Charleston's historic district is beautiful, but has some narrow streets that limit visibility. Drivers must stay alert for other cars, pedestrians and cyclists. Loud music can muffle sirens and horns that distract drivers, making it harder to notice the signs of potential hazards and increasing accident risks.

Heavy Tourist Traffic

Tourist traffic in Charleston can create unpredictable driving conditions. Visitors may not be familiar with local road rules or the flow of traffic, particularly if they end up on one of the many one-way streets. Loud music can distract drivers from adapting to these unpredictable patterns, making it harder to navigate safely through busy downtown areas.

Pedestrian-Friendly Zones

Charleston is known for its vibrant pedestrian zones, including Broad Street and Rainbow Row. Pedestrian-heavy areas require extra vigilance. Drivers playing loud music might not notice pedestrians crossing streets or walking near the road, increasing the risk of pedestrian accidents.

How to Reduce Car Crash Related to Loud Music

Understanding the risks of loud music is the first step toward safer driving. Here are practical strategies to mitigate these risks:

Keep Volume at a Safe Level

One of the simplest ways to reduce the risks associated with loud music is to keep the volume at a moderate level. Ensure that the music does not overpower important sounds from the environment. The general recommendation is to keep the volume low enough so that you can hear sirens and other critical auditory cues.

Choose Music Wisely

The type of music you listen to can have an impact on your driving. Fast paced or highly energetic music can be more distracting than soothing or instrumental music. Opt for music that is calming and less likely to cause cognitive overload. Instrumental tracks or music with fewer lyrics may be less distracting and help you to maintain focus.

Avoid Distractions While Driving

Adjusting the music or making changes to the audio system while driving can be distracting. Minimize these interactions by setting up your playlist or radio stations before you start driving. If you need to adjust your any settings, pull over safely before doing so.

Be Mindful of Your Well-Being

Your own state of mind and physical condition play a role in how music affects your driving. If you are feeling tired or stressed, loud music can exacerbate these feelings and impair your driving further. Ensure that you are well-rested and in a good mental state before getting behind the wheel.

How Claims May Be Affected in Loud Music Related Car Crashes?

Every case is different. However, if loud music contributes to an accident, it can be a factor in determining liability. In car accident cases, distractions like loud music may be considered when assessing fault. A car accident due to someone being distracted, could mean they are at-fault for the car crash. Since South Carolina is an at-fault state, the driver liable for the crash is responsible for covering your medical expenses and other damages. However, you need to speak to an attorney to know your specific legal options.

Contact Roden Law Today

After a car crash, call our firm to discuss your potential case further. Our lawyers at Roden Law want to help you get the compensation you deserve. We can answer your legal questions during a free consultation. There are no upfront cost or fees to speak to our attorney about the details of your scenario.

posts.before:
Backing-up crashes are a common yet significant issue in places like parking lots. Although some of these crashes can be minor, they could still cause serious injuries, especially if the victim is a pedestrian. Determining who may be liable for damages in these incidents is not always straightforward.

Table of Contents

  • Who Is At-Fault for Backing-Up Crashes in Charleston
  • How Backing-Up Crashes Happen
  • Where Do Backing Crashes Happen?
  • Legal Steps to Take After a Backing-Up Crash
  • Preventing Backing-Up Crashes
  • Need Help with Your Backing-Up Crash Claim? Call Roden Law
Were you injured in a backing=up crash in South Carolina? If so, we want to help you. Call our law offices to speak to one of our experienced Charleston car accident attorneys at Roden Law. This meeting is free,  and there is no obligation to file a claim. This is a great opportunity to discuss your situation with a qualified attorney at our firm and determine your potential legal options.

Request your FREE, no-risk consultation today. 1-844-RESULTS

Who Is At-Fault for Backing-Up Crashes in Charleston?

Most of the time, the party backing up is going to be liable. That said, even backing-up crashes in South Carolina can be complex. Liability is not always clear or straightforward, and sometimes fault may be shared. Here are some of the parties who could be liable for a South Carolina backing-up crash:
  • The driver backing-up or out: Often the primary at-fault party since it is their duty to make sure the path is clear before backing out
  • A driver in the feeder lane: May share fault if they were speeding by to avoid having to wait or were not paying attention
  • The vehicle owner: Might share some fault if they knowingly allowed an incompetent driver to use their car
  • An employer: Could be held liable if the backing-up driver was operating a company vehicle on company time
  • Vehicle manufacturer: May be at fault if a vehicle defect, such as a sudden unintended acceleration (SUA), led to the crash
  • Government entity or property manager: Potentially liable if poor road design or negligent maintenance played a role in causing the incident.

What If I Am Partially to Blame for a Backing-Up Crash in Charleston?

It is not uncommon for two parties to share liability for a backing-up crash. South Carolina follows a modified comparative negligence rule, so you may still be able to recover at least a portion of your damages. The percentage of fault you are assessed with gets deducted from any awarded compensation. You cannot, however, recover compensation if you are more than 50 percent liable. Even if you are 51 percent at fault, you are barred from recovering damages. Right after a crash, it is important that you do not try to determine whether you were at fault. Be honest about what you believe happened, but let crash investigators do their job and figure out other factors that may have led to the crash. posts.before:
Rideshare services, like Uber and Lyft, offer a service of convenience, making it easy to get around Charleston. While most rides end without incident, do you know what legal options you have if you get into a crash involving a rideshare driver?

Table of Contents

  • Who Is Liable for a Rideshare Crash?
  • Who Pays for My Damages?

  • How Long Do I Have to File a Legal Claim?
  • Were You Involved in a Rideshare Crash? Speak With a Roden Law Attorney
If you were hurt in a crash involving a rideshare driver, you may wonder what legal options you have for recovering compensation. At Roden Law, we understand your concerns, and we can help answer your questions. Call our Charleston car crash lawyers to discuss your situation — there is no cost for an initial consultation — and learn whether you may have a case.

Request your FREE consultation today at 1-844-RESULTS.

Who Is Liable for a Rideshare Crash?

There are many contributing factors that impact who may be liable in rideshare crashes. To start with, it is important to determine what happened, which is why investigators carefully examine the crash scene and talk to the drivers involved. They will also get statements from any witnesses who saw the crash as it happened. Getting video coverage may be more likely when a rideshare driver is involved. Lyft and Uber drivers sometimes install a dashcam in their vehicles as further protection in the event they are involved in a crash. Depending on the outcome of the investigation and the story the evidence tells, multiple parties could be responsible. Below are some parties who may be fully or partially liable for damages resulting from a rideshare crash:
  • Rideshare Drivers: Uber, Lyft or other rideshare drivers could be liable if their negligence led to the crash that injured you.
  • Other Drivers: Other drivers who hit the Uber or Lyft car you were riding in may be responsible, or at least partially liable for the crash.
  • Vehicle Manufacturer: The manufacturer of a defective rideshare vehicle could be liable if the defect contributed to the crash.
  • Government Entities: Though less common, a local or state agency may be liable if poor road conditions results in a crash, especially if it is due to a lack of maintenance.
  • Rideshare Companies: Uber, Lyft and other rideshare companies might share liability in certain circumstances.

Who Pays for My Damages?

Any compensation you may be eligible for will typically come from the insurance policy of the party or parties deemed liable. In rare cases, it could come from some where else, such as a government entity or another third party. In a rideshare crash, you may be eligible to seek compensation for your medical costs and other damages from the following sources:

Rideshare Company Insurance

Both Uber and Lyft provide insurance coverage for their drivers. The coverage available, however, depends on the driver's status at the time of the accident:
  • If the app was off, the driver's personal insurance applies.
  • If the app was on but no ride had been accepted, the company provides limited liability coverage.
  • If a ride was accepted or a passenger was in the car, the company provides up to $1 million in coverage.

At-Fault Driver's Insurance

If another driver caused the crash, their insurance would be the primary source of compensation.

Your Own Insurance

Your personal auto insurance, might sometimes come into play as well. This is particularly true if the at-fault parties have insufficient coverage or no coverage. In a situation like that, your uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage would help to cover your damages. For instance, say an at-fault driver has some coverage, but it only covers 70 percent of your compensation. If eligible, then you may be able to cover the remaining 30 percent of your damages through your uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage.

Other Liable Parties

If a vehicle manufacturer or government entity is found liable, their insurance or funds would provide compensation.

What Type of Compensation May I Seek from a Rideshare Crash?

Every rideshare crash involves different scenarios, potentially requiring various compensation. In a high impact collision, rideshare passengers may have severe injuries that cause them to need compensation for surgery and other related medical bills. You may be entitled to several types of compensation such as:
  • Medical expenses: This covers emergency treatment, hospital stays, surgeries, medications and future medical care
  • Lost wages: If your injuries cause you to miss work, you can seek compensation for lost income, including future earnings if you're unable to return to your job.
  • Pain and suffering: This non-economic damage compensates for physical pain and emotional distress caused by the accident.
  • Property damage: If your personal property was damaged in the crash, you can seek compensation for repairs or replacement.
  • Loss of enjoyment of life: Compensate for injuries that prevent you from enjoying hobbies or activities, you once did before the crash
  • Punitive damages: Use to punish the wrongdoers in cases of extreme negligence or intentional misconduct

How Long Do I Have to File a Legal Claim?

In Georgia, you have two years from the date of the car crash to file a claim. The legal term for this deadline is the statute of limitations. Two years may sound like a lot of time, but it is important to remember that your attorney needs time to build a solid case. Injured victims who file late in the game give their attorney little time to get optimum results. If you miss the deadline, you will likely be barred from recovering any damages.

Can I Sue After Lyft Driver Hit My Car in Charleston?

Yes, you can sue after a Lyft accident in Charleston. South Carolina law allows accident victims to seek compensation for their injuries and losses.   • Determining Liability: The insurance company or a jury, if you take your case to court, will establish who is at fault for the accident.
  • Insurance Claims: You can file a claim with Lyft required insurance coverage once liability is determined to pay for damages and injuries.
  • Legal Action: If Lyft’s insurance claim does not cover all your damages, you can file a lawsuit against the driver or Lyft.

How Can I Prove Fault in a Charleston Red Light Lyft Accident?

After a Lyft driver hits, your car, you need to prove the Lyft driver was at fault. Evidence that can help establish fault includes:
  • Police reports
  • Traffic camera footage
  • Dashcam Footage
  • Eyewitness statements
  • Cell phone records
  • Vehicle Damage Report

Rideshare accident cases present unique challenges. For example. If there are multiple parties involved in a car accident, various perspective can make it difficult to determine who is a fault. Lyft’s insurance coverage varies depending on whether a driver was logged into the app, waiting for a ride request or carrying a passenger. You will have to prove the Lyft driver was logged into the app during the time of the accident to get a claim from Lyft. If not, you may have to file a claim with the driver’s personal auto insurance. Other legal challenges you may face could include:
  • Navigating multiple insurance policies especially if the Lyft driver does not have enough personal insurance to cover your damages and you cannot receive a claim from Lyft insurance.
  • Lyft may have a strong legal representation, making it challenging to negotiate a fair settlement or win a lawsuit.

What Are Some Common Reasons a Lyft Driver May Run a Red Light?

A Lyft driver could run a red light and hit your car for several reasons. Common causes of this behavior are likely to happen if a Lyft driver experiences any of the following.
  • Distracted Driving: If drivers are using their phone for navigation or communicating with passengers, they could miss traffic signals.
  • Fatigue: Some drivers may work long hours causing them to become exhausted and have a slower reaction time.
  • Speeding: The more rides that a Lyft driver takes, the more money they make. Some drivers may speed to complete more rides, which could tempt them to run a red light
  • Impatience or Running Late: If a driver is running late, they might become drive more aggressively so they can hurry to pick up or drop off passengers.
  • Impairment: Some drivers may be under the influence of alcohol or drugs which could significantly impact their ability to obey traffic signals.
  • Unfamiliarity With the Area: Drivers who are not familiar with a traffic pattern in a location could make the sudden decision to run a red light.

posts.before:
A car crash that causes permanent injuries creates lifelong challenges. Victims face significant emotional and physical changes that impact their daily quality of life, along with mounting medical bills. Many car crash survivors in this situation may wonder if they have a claim, what it could be worth and how much compensation they can recover to help pay for continuing medical treatments, lost wages and other damages.

  • What Permanent Injuries May Result From a Car Accident?
  • How Do I Calculate the Value of My Charleston Car Accident Claim?
  • Injured in a Car Crash? Seek Legal Help From Our Trusted Law Firm
If you were injured in a car crash, you may be entitled to significant compensation for your damages. Learn more about the factors that impact the overall value of your claim. Need legal help after a South Carolina car accident? At Roden Law, we are dedicated to holding at-fault parties accountable and recovering the maximum possible compensation for our clients. Learn about your potential legal options when you speak to one of our experienced car accident lawyers in Charleston. We fight hard to get you the results you need, and there are no upfront costs or fees to pay.

Call to Request your free consultation today: 1-844-RESULTS

What Permanent Injuries May Result From a Car Accident?

A permanent injury is one that does not heal completely, or a condition that will continue to affect you for the rest of your life. These types of injuries often lead to chronic pain, loss of function and in some cases, permanent disability. Some common examples of permanent injuries sustained in car accidents include:
  • Traumatic brain injuries affecting cognitive function
  • Spinal cord damage leading to paralysis
  • Severe burns causing disfigurement
  • Loss of limbs requiring prosthetics
  • Joint injuries resulting in chronic pain
  • Vision or hearing loss
  • Nerve damage causing persistent numbness
The impact of these injuries extends beyond just physical pain. Many people with permanent injuries face challenges related to employment, personal relationships and daily activities. Some may need lifelong medical care, assistive devices or ongoing therapy.

How Do I Calculate the Value of My Charleston Car Accident Claim?

While every car accident case is different, permanent injury settlements could range from hundreds of thousands or more. Factors impacting the overall value of your claim include:

Extent and Severity of Your Injuries

The more severe and permanent the injury, the higher the potential value of your claim. For example, an amputation or paralysis will typically result in a much larger settlement compared to a broken bone that heals within a few months. If your injuries cause permanent disability, requiring ongoing care or preventing you from working, the value of your claim will reflect these long-term consequences.

Medical Expenses

The cost of medical treatment after a car crash plays a significant role when determining the value of your claim. For permanent injuries, treatment costs can add up quickly and may include:
  • Emergency care immediately following the accident
  • Diagnostic testing
  • Surgery or other major medical procedures
  • Long-term physical therapy
  • Assistive devices (e.g., wheelchairs, prosthetics)
  • Pain management
  • Home healthcare services
  • Rehabilitation therapy
  • Pain and suffering
In South Carolina, victims can recover compensation for past, present and future medical expenses. If your injuries require lifelong medical treatment, this can significantly increase the value of your claim.

Lost Wages and Loss of Earning Capacity

If your permanent injuries prevent you from working or significantly limit the type of work you can perform, you are entitled to compensation for lost wages. This includes both the wages you have already lost and the wages you will lose in the future. The longer the impact of your injury on your ability to earn a living, the more compensation you may be able to claim for loss of earning capacity. If your injury limits your ability to work in the same field or results in a permanent reduction in income, the value of your claim will reflect this financial loss.

Pain and Suffering

Pain and suffering is a non-economic damage that compensates you for the physical pain, emotional distress and reduced quality of life caused by your injuries. Unlike medical expenses, pain and suffering damages do not have an exact formula. However, the more severe and permanent the injury, the higher the potential compensation. Some of the pain and suffering factors that may influence the value of your claim include:
  • The intensity and duration of pain
  • Whether you will experience ongoing pain for the rest of your life
  • The emotional toll of living with a permanent disability
  • The impact the injury has on your mental health (depression, anxiety, PTSD)
  • The way your injury affects your ability to participate in normal activities or enjoy life

Impact on Daily Life and Relationships

Permanent injuries often lead to changes in a person’s daily life, including a reduced ability to perform everyday tasks, like driving, cooking or caring for children. The ability to engage in social, recreational or family activities may be severely impacted. The more your injury alters your ability to live a normal, fulfilling life, the greater the value of your claim. Additionally, how your injury affects your relationships with your spouse, children or other close family members should be factored into your compensation.

Insurance Coverage and Liability

The amount of insurance coverage the at-fault driver carries affects the value of your claim as well. South Carolina law requires drivers to carry a minimum of $25,000 in liability insurance per person and $50,000 per accident for bodily injury. However, if the at-fault driver is underinsured or uninsured, this can complicate the claims process. If you have uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage, your own insurance policy may come into play. In some cases, these policies can help cover the costs of permanent injuries when the at-fault driver has insufficient coverage.

Injured in a Car Crash? Seek Legal Help From Our Trusted Law Firm

If you are dealing with permanent injuries after a car crash, we recommend seeking legal counsel as soon as possible. Trying to establish the other party's fault, calculating the value of your claim and negotiating your settlement is not something you should attempt alone. At Roden Law, our legal team has extensive experience managing these type of cases, we have a history of proven results, and there are no upfront costs or fees to pay. We want you to focus on your health and recovery. Let us fight to recover the full compensation you deserve. We are here to help you.

What Is Brake Failure and Its Role in Rideshare Accidents?

Brake failure can occur for many reasons. While it is often the result of mechanical malfunction, it can also be due to inadequate maintenance or manufacturer defects. Some common causes of brake failure include:
  • Worn-out brake pads or rotors
  • Low brake fluid
  • Defective brake components (e.g., master cylinder, brake calipers)
  • Improperly maintained brakes
  • Faulty brake lines
  • Manufacturer defects in the braking system
When a rideshare driver loses control due to brake failure, they may not be able to avoid a crash or stop safely. This could lead to passengers sustaining injuries. In some crashes, drivers and pedestrians could get hurt. Brake failure accidents are particularly dangerous because they can occur without warning, leaving little time for reaction.

Who May Be Liable for Brake Failure in Rideshare Collisions?

One of the challenges of pursuing compensation after a rideshare accident is understanding which party or parties may be liable. If an at-fault driver negligence leads to a car accident, this individual is usually held responsible. However, in the case of brake failure, liability could extend to several parties.

The Rideshare Driver

A rideshare driver may not always be directly or solely responsible for the brake failure. However, they are still required toe of the crash, the company may be responsible for damages caused by the accident. In addition, if the rideshare company failed to ensure that their drivers’ vehicles were properly maintained, they could be partially at fault.

The Vehicle Manufacturer

operate a vehicle safely. If the driver neglected proper vehicle maintenance or failed to address known issues with the vehicle, they may bear some responsibility.

The Rideshare Company (Uber, Lyft, etc.)

Rideshare companies like Uber and Lyft may be held liable under certain conditions. If the driver was working for the company at the time of the crash, the company may be responsible for damages caused by the accident. In addition, if the rideshare company failed to ensure that their drivers’ vehicles were properly maintained, they could be partially at fault. If the brake failure was due to a problem with the vehicle’s braking system, the manufacturer could be held responsible. This could happen if there was a flaw in the design, manufacturing, or quality control of the vehicle or its parts, which led to a malfunction and ultimately caused the accident.

Vehicle Maintenance Provider

If the vehicle was not properly maintained or repaired, the mechanic or repair shop that worked on it could be held responsible. This might happen if they missed a faulty brake part during a routine inspection.

What Steps Should I Take After a Rideshare Crash?

After a rideshare crash, there are key steps you need to take to protect your rights and strengthen your case for compensation. These steps are important whether you were a passenger in the rideshare vehicle or a rideshare driver hit your vehicle.

Check for Injuries

First, check for any injuries at the crash scene and call for medical help if needed. Even if you feel fine, it is still a good idea to get checked by a doctor, as some injuries may not be immediately obvious. It is important to see a doctor after any accident. Injuries like whiplash, back pain or head trauma may not be immediately apparent. Waiting too long to seek treatment can also hurt your chances of making a successful injury claim later.

Call the Police

It is essential to report the accident to the police, especially if there are injuries or significant property damage. The police report will be a vital document in establishing the facts of the case and may note important details, such as how the crash happened due to brake failure.

Document the Scene

Take photographs of the accident scene, including the vehicles involved, visible damage to the brakes or other vehicle parts and any road conditions that could have contributed to the crash. Record your injuries and damage to any personal property, like your phone or clothing. Be sure to collect contact details from any witnesses who saw the crash.

Notify the Rideshare Company

If you were a passenger, notify the rideshare company (Uber, Lyft, etc.) as soon as possible. They have specific procedures for handling accidents and may launch an investigation. Make sure to file an incident report and request a copy for your records.

What Are Delayed Injuries After a Car Crash

Delayed injuries are medical conditions that do not present symptoms immediately after a car accident. These injuries can emerge hours, days or even weeks after a collision. The human body's complex response to trauma along with adrenaline and shock, can mask pain and other injury symptoms. Common delayed injuries include:
  • Traumatic brain injuries that develop gradually
  • Soft tissue damage in muscles and ligaments
  • Whiplash-related to neck and spine complications
  • Internal bleeding or organ damage
  • Psychological trauma like post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
  • Concussions and delayed neurological symptoms
  • Herniated discs that worsen over time
The absence of immediate pain does not mean you are uninjured. Professional medical diagnostic tests are crucial to rule out any serious medical conditions. Even if you feel fine initially, it is a good idea to seek medical attention immediately.

How Delayed Injuries Affect Your Car Crash Claim

Delayed injuries can significantly complicate the legal process of seeking compensation. Insurance companies often scrutinize claims where injuries are not immediately reported or documented. This makes understanding and properly addressing delayed injuries critical to protecting your legal rights. Key factors you should know about delayed injuries and filing claims include:
  • Medical documentation becomes paramount in proving your injuries
  • Waiting too long to seek medical treatment can weaken your claim
  • Insurance adjusters may argue that your injuries are unrelated to the accident
  • South Carolina's statute of limitations requires timely filing with complete medical evidence.
  • Financial compensation depends on detailed medical evidence

Proving Delayed Injuries for Your Claim

Successfully documenting delayed injuries requires taking the appropriate steps. It is important to file your claim with a licensed attorney that have experience with car accident cases because they can help you throughout the legal process. Some of the ways that you can strengthen your case if you have delayed injuries may involve:
  • Requesting Medical Records: If you go to the doctor and find out that you have injuries, get a copy of your medical records. Documents created close to the accident date serve as crucial evidence.
  • Documenting Medical Bills and Treatment: Keep a paper trail of your doctor appointments, prescriptions and any treatment related to your accident injuries. Preserve all medical bills, diagnostic reports and physician notes.
  • Follow Complete Treatment Plans: Adhere strictly to your healthcare provider's recommended treatment plan. Gaps in treatment can be used by insurance companies to challenge the severity of your injuries.
  • Keep a Personal Injury Journal: Record daily pain levels, medical treatments, emotional impacts and how injuries affect your work and personal life. Detailed documentation provides powerful narrative evidence.
  • Consult Medical Specialists: Some injuries require additional insight from neurologists, orthopedic surgeons,  and other medical professionals. These individuals can provide detailed assessments of the extent and severity of your injuries.

What Are the Long-Term Health Effects of Delayed Injuries?

Delayed injuries can have lasting impact beyond immediate medical concerns. Many victims underestimate the potential long-term health and financial consequences of seemingly minor post-accident symptoms. Some car crash victims may ignore injuries, assuming they will resolve with the treatment they are already receiving from their doctor. However, this assumption can result in delayed injuries going untreated. If you notice any new symptoms while being treated for existing car crash injuries, be sure to inform your doctor. They may need to create a new treatment plan or adjust your current one. Chronic pain, neurological complications and psychological trauma can develop months or even years after a car crash. These conditions may require extensive medical treatment, rehabilitation, and ongoing care, significantly disrupting your personal and professional life. Additionally, some delayed injuries can lead to permanent disability, affecting your future earning capacity and overall quality of life. Proactively documenting medical interactions, tracking symptom progression and working with medical professionals can help you receive appropriate care and support for a full recovery.

posts.before:
Most drivers understand the dangers of driving under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs. However, many people do not realize that driving under the influence of prescription medications can be equally dangerous.

Table of Contents

  • How Can Prescription Medication Affect My Driving?

  • Call Roden Law After You Have Been Involved in a Car Accident
Discover how prescribed medications can impact your driving ability. Below, our Charleston car accident lawyers discusses the types of prescription medication that could lead to car accidents and steps to take if you are involved in a car accident with a driver under the influence of prescription medication. If you have been injured in a car crash, seek medical attention immediately and legal counsel from a trusted attorney. At Roden Law, we can help you determine your legal options so that you can pursue legal actions.

Request your FREE case review today: 1-844-RESULTS.

How Can Prescription Medication Affect My Driving?

Effects from prescription medication can cause drivers to swerve in and out of lanes or loose control of their vehicle. Even medications prescribed by trusted healthcare professionals can create dangerous driving conditions if not carefully managed. Prescription medications can significantly impair driving performance by:
  • Causing drowsiness or sedation
  • Reducing reaction times
  • Blurring vision
  • Causing dizziness
  • Impairing cognitive function
  • Decreasing motor coordination

What Types of Prescription Medication Could Lead to a Car Accident?

Several categories of prescription medications can compromise driving safety, such as:
  • Opioids: Used for managing pain and can cause drowsiness, slowed reaction times and impaired coordination.
  • Benzodiazepines: Medications like Xanax and Valium could be prescribed for anxiety and insomnia, which can lead to drowsiness, dizziness and poor judgment.
  • Antidepressants: Antidepressants like Prozac and Zoloft are used to treat depression but can lead to dizziness or blurred vision.
  • Antihistamines: This medication is used for allergies and cold symptoms. Drugs like Benadryl can cause drowsiness and reduced concentration.
  • Sleep Medications: Medication for individuals who have trouble sleeping can cause drivers to feel drowsy. For example, Ambien is a common sleep medication that is known for increasing the risk of accidents.

What Symptoms Could Lead to an Accident After Taking Prescription Medication?

Recognizing potential driving risks involves understanding specific symptoms:
  • Excessive yawning or feeling extremely tired
  • Difficulty maintaining lane position
  • Delayed reaction to traffic signals or sudden movements
  • Feeling disconnected or "foggy"
  • Feeling unusually relaxed or disoriented

Is It Illegal To Drive After Taking Prescription Medication?

In South Carolina, driving under the influence (DUI) laws still apply to prescription medications if they impair your ability to drive safely. While having a valid prescription is legal, driving while impaired is not. Under Section 56-5-2930, this law states that it is illegal to drive a vehicle under the influence of any substance, including prescription medication, if it impairs your ability to drive safely. Even with a valid prescription, you can be legally responsible if your medication causes a car accident. Law enforcement can still charge you with:
  • Driving under the influence
  • Reckless driving
  • Negligent operation of a vehicle

What Should I Do if I'm Injured Due to a Driver Being on Prescribed Medication?

Proving medication-related impairment requires thorough investigation and gathering evidence. If you have been injured in a car crash because another driver was impaired from prescribe medication, it is highly recommended to seek medical attention and reach out to a licensed car accident attorney. They can help you with filing a claim and navigating the complex legal process. If you have been involved in an accident potentially caused by prescription medication, take these steps:
  • Document everything at the accident scene
  • Get diagnostic tests for your injuries
  • Collect contact information from witnesses
  • Request a copy of the police report
  • Keep all medical records

How Can Drivers Prevent Driving Under the Influence of Prescription Medication?

Before drivers operate a vehicle, it is important that they know the preventative measures that they need to take to avoid any road hazards. Some steps that can be taken to prevent impaired driving due to prescription medications are:

Understanding Your Medication

Always read the label and warnings on your prescription medications. Look for any indications that the medication may cause drowsiness, dizziness or impair your ability to drive.

Consult Your Doctor

Ask your healthcare if your medication might affect your driving. They can provide you with guidance on when to take your medication and whether it is safe to drive while under certain medications.

Monitor Your Reaction

Everyone’s body react differently to medication. Pay attention to how you feel after taking your medication. If you experience any symptoms such as drowsiness or blurred vision, avoid driving.

Avoid Mixing Medication

Be cautious about taking multiple medications at once. Sometimes the combination of multiple medications could increase the risk of impairment. Also, avoid mixing medication with alcohol as it can cause you to become impaired before you drive.

Plan Ahead

If you know that you have to take medication that could impair your ability to drive, take alternative transportation like Uber, a public transit or ask a friend or family member for a ride.

Stay Informed

Stay up to date with any new information about your medications and their potential side effects. Your pharmacist can provide you with resourceful information.

Why Am I So Tired After My Charleston Car Crash?

After a car crash, your body undergoes physical and emotional stress, which can lead to extreme fatigue. Injuries, even those that seem minor, can drain your energy as your body works to heal. Adrenaline and shock from the accident can mask pain initially, but once those effects wear off, exhaustion can set in. Additionally, anxiety, sleep disturbances and the stress from dealing with accident-related matters can contribute to feeling overly tired. Fatigue can also be linked to internal injuries that might not be immediately apparent, such as whiplash, concussions or soft tissue damage. These injuries can disrupt your normal sleep patterns and cause lingering pain, both of which are major contributors to post-accident exhaustion.

When Should I See a Doctor About Car Crash Fatigue?

You should see a doctor if your fatigue after a car crash lasts longer than a few days or if it is affecting your ability to function normally. Here are some signs that indicate it is time to seek medical attention:
  • Fatigue lasts more than a few days
  • You have trouble working or completing daily tasks
  • You experience headaches, dizziness or memory problems
  • Sleep disturbances or trouble resting
  • Fatigue worsens or does not improve over time
  • You notice new or increasing pain alongside fatigue

What Injuries Could Make Me Feel Unusually Tired?

Identifying these hidden injuries can help explain your exhaustion and guide you toward the right treatment.

Whiplash and Soft Tissue Injuries

Whiplash and other soft tissue injuries can cause pain and stiffness, leading to exhaustion as your body works to heal. Some other symptoms of whiplash and soft tissue injuries may include limited motion in the neck area and headaches.

Concussions or Mild Traumatic Brain Injury

Even a mild concussion can disrupt sleep patterns and cause fatigue, headaches and difficulty concentrating. After a concussion or any head injury, the brain requires more energy to heal. This demand for energy can result in physical and mental exhaustion. Additionally, a concussion, could cause sleep disturbance such as insomnia or excessive sleepiness.

Internal Injuries

Internal injuries, such as damage to organs or blood vessels, may not show symptoms right away but can lead to fatigue as your body responds to the trauma. For instance, blood loss from internal bleeding reduces oxygen circulation, leading to fatigue.

Spinal Injuries

Damage to the spine, including misalignments or nerve compression, can cause chronic pain and fatigue. Spinal injuries that affect nerve pathways can disrupt normal muscle functions and sensory signals, making daily activities more strenuous. The constant strain of compensating for spinal injuries can deplete a car crash victim’s energy, leading to poor sleep quality and persistent exhaustion.

How Long Could Fatigue Last After a Car Accident?

How long post-accident fatigue lasts varies from person to person, depending on the severity of your injuries and how your body is healing. For some people, fatigue may only last a few days or weeks as the body recovers from injuries and the traumatic experience of being in a car accident. However, if you sustained severe internal injuries, like whiplash or a concussion, you may also continue to feel tired. If you continue to feel fatigued for more than a couple of days, you should seek additional medical attention to rule out more serious injuries and/or get the treatment you need.

How Does Post-Accident Fatigue Affect Your Injury Claim?

Post-accident fatigue can have a significant impact on your injury claim in many ways. To begin with, if it is a sign of other injuries, you will likely need additional treatment, which is costly. Fatigue can also affect your ability to get through a work day or even do simple household tasks. Getting the treatment you need as soon as possible can make a difference not only in your ability to fully recover, but also in ensuring those damages are included in the overall value of your claim so you can be compensated fairly.

Impact on Work and Earning Capacity

Fatigue can make it difficult to return to work or perform job duties, which can affect your earning capacity and overall financial stability. You may not be able to complete certain tasks within a timely manner like you once did before the accident. This could mean that you may have to switch to a job in another industry, especially if you have permanent injuries.

Difficulty in Documenting Symptoms

Fatigue can also make it harder to track and document your symptoms, which is crucial for proving the extent of your injuries. For example, fatigue could mask injuries like sprains, fractures and concussions, causing victims to not detect symptoms for these injuries right away.

Medical Evidence

Consistent medical records showing how fatigue has impacted your life helps to strengthen your claim. However, if you have not sought treatment or have missed follow-up appointments, you may not have the evidence needed to prove that fatigue is linked to a car crash or that it exists. As a result, you may not get the full compensation that you need to recover from these injuries.

Why Am I So Tired After My Charleston Car Crash?

After a car crash, your body undergoes physical and emotional stress, which can lead to extreme fatigue. Injuries, even those that seem minor, can drain your energy as your body works to heal. Adrenaline and shock from the accident can mask pain initially, but once those effects wear off, exhaustion can set in. Additionally, anxiety, sleep disturbances and the stress from dealing with accident-related matters can contribute to feeling overly tired. When Should I See a Doctor About Car Crash Fatigue?

You should see a doctor if your fatigue after a car crash lasts longer than a few days or if it is affecting your ability to function normally. Here are some signs that indicate it is time to seek medical attention:
  • Fatigue lasts more than a few days
  • You have trouble working or completing daily tasks

Whiplash and Soft Tissue Injuries

Concussions or Mild Traumatic Brain Injury

Even a mild concussion can disrupt sleep patterns and cause fatigue, headaches and difficulty concentrating. After a concussion or any head injury, the brain requires more energy to heal. This demand for energy can result in physical and mental exhaustion. Additionally, a concussion, could cause sleep disturbance such as insomnia or excessive sleepiness.

Internal Injuries

Internal injuries, such as damage to organs or blood vessels, may not show symptoms right away but can lead to fatigue as your body responds to the trauma. For instance, blood loss from internal bleeding reduces oxygen circulation, leading to fatigue.

Spinal Injuries

Damage to the spine, including misalignments or nerve compression, can cause chronic pain and fatigue. posts.before:
After a car accident, seeking immediate medical attention is necessary for your health and legal claim. While you have the right to refuse medical treatment, this decision could significantly impact your ability to recover compensation for your injuries.

  • Do I Have the Right To Refuse Certain Medical Treatment?

If you have been injured in a car accident and decline medical treatment, seek counsel from a licensed attorney before you go through with your decision. A trusted Charleston car accident attorney can help you navigate through the legal process.
