Do I Have the Right To Refuse Certain Medical Treatment?

Yes, you absolutely have the legal right to refuse medical treatment after a car accident. This right is protected under both state and federal law, stemming from the fundamental principle of bodily autonomy. However, understanding the consequences of this decision is essential. Medical professionals recommend treatment to ensure your well-being and document any injuries diagnosed as a result of a car accident. Even if you do not think you have any injuries seek medical attention. Some injuries may not be apparent right away. Injuries like whiplash or internal bleeding can have delayed symptoms that worsen over time. When you refuse medical treatment, you might be putting both your health and your legal right at risk.

How Can Refusing Medical Treatment Impact My Claim?

The decision to refuse medical treatment can have profound consequences for your car accident claim. Insurance companies and defense attorneys will scrutinize every aspect of your case, including your medical decisions.

Weakens Your Injury Claim Evidence

Medical documentation serves as crucial evidence in personal injury cases. When you seek immediate medical attention, healthcare providers create detailed records that gives insight into your injuries, treatment plans and prognosis. These records establish a clear link between the accident and your injuries, strengthening your claim. Without this documentation, proving the extent and cause of your injuries becomes significantly more challenging.

No Evidence for Pain and Suffering

Medical records provide objective evidence of your pain and suffering. For example, they can give insight into why you have chronic pain and how difficult your physical therapy appointments are. When you refuse treatment, you lose the opportunity to have professional documentation of your condition immediately after the accident, which can be difficult to reconstruct later.

Gives Insurers Reason To Deny Payment

Insurance companies are always looking for reasons to minimize or deny claims. Refusing medical treatment gives them powerful ammunition to argue that your injuries were not serious or were not caused by the accident. They might insist that if you were truly injured, you would have sought immediate medical attention. Insurance adjusters may also argue that your injuries worsened because you did not seek prompt medical care, making you partially responsible for your current condition. Their assumptions could lead to claims denial.

Decrease the Value of Your Claim

When calculating the value of your claim, insurance companies and courts look at various factors, including the promptness and consistency of your medical treatment. Refusing treatment can significantly decrease your claim's value because:
  • The gap between the accident and your eventual treatment makes it harder to prove causation
  • Your injuries may have worsened, but the insurer can argue this was due to your negligence in seeking treatment
  • The lack of immediate medical documentation makes it difficult to establish the initial severity of your injuries

What Evidence Should I Gather if I Refuse Medical Treatment After a Car Crash?

If you refuse medical treatment after a car crash, it can be more challenging to prove your injuries and claim compensation. However, you can still gather other evidence to support your case, such as:
  • Police Report: This document provides an official account of the incident and can help establish fault.
  • Photographs and Videos: Visual evidence can help demonstrate the severity of the crash.
  • Witness Statements: Witnesses account of what happened at the car crash scene can align with your version of events, which can help strengthen your case.
  • Receipts and Bills: Save all your receipts related to expenses incurred due to the accident, like vehicle repairs, transportation costs, and any over-the-counter medications or treatment you purchased.
  • Employment Records: Document any time missed from work and any impact on your ability to perform your job. This could show the financial impact the accident had on your injuries.

Reasons Car Crash Victims Refuse Treatment

Car crash victims may refuse medical treatment for several reasons. Sometimes victims may refuse treatment if they have a suspicion or a concern that they think may hinder them. Common reasons include:
  • Fear of missing work or losing income
  • Anxiety about medical procedures or hospitals
  • Belief that injuries are minor and will heal on their own
  • Religious or personal beliefs about certain medical treatments
  • Financial concerns about medical bills and lack of insurance coverage
While these concerns are valid, it is important to remember that delaying or refusing medical treatment can cost you more in the long run, both in terms of your health and your legal claim. Most personal injury attorneys can help you find medical providers who will treat you on a lien basis, meaning they will wait for payment until your case settles.

  • Call Roden Law if You Have a Shoulder Injury After a Car Accident
If you have suffered a shoulder injury in a Charleston car crash due to someone else's negligence, you have the right to seek compensation for your damages. Understanding the nature of your injury, its potential long-term effects and your legal options is essential for protecting your right and securing fair compensation. At Roden Law, our Charleston car accident attorneys are here to help you through the legal process so you can focus on your recovery. What Is the Most Common Shoulder Injury From a Car Accident?

Car accidents frequently cause various shoulder injuries, with rotator cuff tears being the most common. The rotator cuff consists of four muscles and tendons that stabilize your shoulder joint and enable arm movement. During a collision, the sudden impact can cause these tissues to stretch, tear or become severely damaged. While rotator cuff injuries are one of the most frequent injuries, other common shoulder injuries from car accidents include:
  • Shoulder Fractures: Breaks in the bones of the shoulder can cause victims to experience severe pain, swelling and difficulty moving the arm.
  • Shoulder Dislocation: This occurs when the upper arm bone pops out of the shoulder socket, causing intense pain and limited mobility.
  • Labral Tears: The labrum is a ring of cartilage that surrounds the shoulder socket and helps keep the joint stable. Tears in this cartilage can lead to pain and instability in the shoulder.
  • Bursitis: This involves inflammation of small, fluid-filled sacs that cushion your joints and reduce friction between bones, tendons and muscles. This may lead to pain and swelling, particularly during arm movement.
  • AC Joint Separation: This may happen when the joint connecting your collarbone to shoulder blade becomes damaged due to a fall or direct blow to the shoulder, leading to a visible bump on the shoulder.
Shoulder injuries occur when the body is thrown forward during impact, especially if you are gripping the steering wheel tightly. Side-impact collisions can also cause direct trauma to the shoulder area.

How Do I Know if My Shoulder Injuries Are Severe?

Recognizing the severity of a shoulder injury early can ensure you receive proper treatment and detailed documentation for your injury claim. Warning signs of a serious shoulder injury include:
  • Visible deformity or swelling
  • Weakness in the arm or shoulder
  • Bruising around the shoulder area
  • Inability to raise your arm above your head
  • Inability to raise your arm above your head
  • Pain that worsens at night or prevents sleep
  • Numbness or tingling extending down your arm
  • A popping or grinding sensation when moving your shoulder
Do not dismiss these symptoms as minor or temporary. Some shoulder injuries may seem manageable initially but can become worse without proper medical attention. Additionally, adrenaline released during the accident can mask pain, making injuries appear less severe than they are.

What Evidence Can Link My Shoulder Injury to the Car Accident?

Building a strong connection between your shoulder injury and the car accident requires solid evidence. Below are the types of evidence that can help link your injuries to the accident.

Medical Documentation

If you go to the emergency room or urgent care, be sure that you obtain records that shows details of your injuries. Documents show immediate care after a car accident, prove the severity of your injuries and could indicate the type of medical treatment you will need to recover. Other medical documentations you may use as evidence may include:
  • Physical therapy records
  • Treatment plans and physician notes
  • Documentation of any surgical procedures
  • Diagnostic imaging results (X-rays, MRI, CT scans)

Accident-Related Evidence

A police report detailing the crash circumstances can help indicate who was at fault. Photographs of the accident scene may show the point of impact and how the crash occurred. If you could not take photos at the scene, check for video footage from nearby surveillance cameras or dashcams, including your own or another driver’s. If any witnesses observe the accident, they can provide statements describing the collision. This evidence strengthen your case, especially when witnesses account of what happened aligns with your perspective of how the accident happened. After you take your vehicle to the repair shop, be sure to get a repair estimate so that it may be added into your compensation. It is a good idea to have any evidence that shows damages to your property so that you may receive compensation for it.

Expert Testimony

Testimony from medical experts and accident reconstruction specialists can provide valuable insight into the car crash. A medical professional can explain the extent and severity of your injuries. When the cause of a crash is not clear, we may consult with an accident reconstruction specialist. These specially trained professionals examine the same evidence, but they use scientific methods combined with high tech tools to recreate the crash. These crash scene recreations often clarify complex crashes and help to establish who is at-fault. Some car crash victims may have challenges with going back to work after a collision. As a result, they can miss work or may have a reduced earning capacity if they can not return to the same type of work they were used to doing before the car accident. An occupational professional can describe how your injury affects your ability to work so that you may receive compensation for lost wages, future earning potential and diminished capacity to perform your job. Their testimony can ensure you have a solid case and help ensure you receive fair compensation for the financial impact of your injuries.

How Much Compensation Can I Receive for My Shoulder Injuries?

Every case is different; therefore, the compensation amount may vary depending on the severity of the injury, duration it takes to recover and how the crash impact on your daily activities. It is recommended to speak to a licensed attorney to get a better understanding of your injuries. They can determine your case value based on the specific, unique details and events of your case. Below are the type of compensation you may be eligible for after sustaining a shoulder injury in a car crash.

Economic Damages

Economic damages are the types of compensation that is related to monetary value. Examples of economic damages include:
  • Lost wages during recovery
  • Current and future medical expenses
  • Physical therapy and rehabilitation costs
  • Transportation expenses for medical appointments
  • Reduced earning capacity if the injury affects your ability to work

Non-Economic Damages

Non-economic damages focus on compensating car crash victims for the intangible losses that resulted from an injury. Some of these non-economic damages are:
  • Pain and suffering
  • Emotional distress
  • Loss of enjoyment of life
  • Impact on personal relationships
  • Physical impairment or disfigurement

Inform your doctor about any pre-existing conditions or previous injuries, particularly those involving the same areas affected in your recent accident. What Is a Traumatic Brain Injury?

A Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) occurs when a sudden trauma causes damage to the brain. This damage can result from the head violently hitting an object, an object piercing the skull and entering brain tissue or forces that cause the brain to move within the skull, such as violent shaking or blast waves.

How Do Car Crashes Cause Serious Brain Injuries?

Car crashes can cause severe brain injuries through several types of incidents that happen during a car crash. Some incidents may include:
  • Direct Impact Trauma: When the head strikes objects like the steering wheel, windshield, or side window, the force can fracture the skull and damage brain tissue directly.
  • Acceleration-Deceleration Forces: Even without direct head impact, rapid acceleration and deceleration causes the brain to collide with the inner skull wall. This creates bruising (contusions) and tearing of nerve fibers (diffuse axonal injury).
  • Penetrating Injuries: Broken glass, metal fragments or other debris can pierce the skull and enter brain tissue.

Car Crashes Factors Affecting Severity of Injuries

The severity of injuries depends on factors like the vehicle speed at impact and the direction of the collision. If a car crash victim did not wear a seat belt, it could increase the severity of their injuries. In some cases, passengers sitting in the front of the vehicle are more likely to suffer from more serious injuries. Older cars with fewer safety features than newer cars could have higher impacts, which may result in more severe injuries.

Secondary Injuries Worsening Health Conditions

Secondary injuries often develop after the initial trauma due to brain swelling or internal bleeding. These injuries frequently affect vital brain regions that control movement, cognition, speech and other vital functions. Prompt medical treatment is essential to prevent worsening damage and improve recovery outcomes.

What Types of Traumatic Brain Injuries Are Common in Car Crashes?

The violent forces involved in collisions can damage the brain in various ways, from mild concussions to severe trauma requiring intensive medical intervention. Victims should know the different types of brain injuries that can happen in a car crash to help with their recovery, a potential legal case and to navigate through life-altering conditions.

Concussions

A concussion is a type of traumatic brain injury that is caused when your brain collides with the inside of your skull. During a car crash, the sudden stop or impact forces cause your brain to bounce or twist inside the skull. Some of the key symptoms of a concussion:
  • Headaches
  • Confusion
  • Memory problems
  • Vision changes
  • Balance issues
  • Nausea
  • Sensitivity to light/noise
  • Sleep disturbances

Hematomas and Hemorrhages

A violent car crash can tear blood vessels in your brain, leading to two types of life-threatening conditions. One is a hematoma, which occurs when blood collects between your brain and skull, creating dangerous pressure on delicate brain tissue. These blood pools may develop slowly over hours or days after the accident, making them particularly dangerous. Brain hemorrhages present a greater threat, as active bleeding within the brain tissue itself can cause rapid deterioration. The bleeding damages surrounding brain cells and creates swelling that can lead to permanent injury or death without immediate treatment. After any head impact, watch out for severe headaches that intensify, growing confusion, slurred speech and seizures.

Brain Contusions

A brain contusion is bruising of brain tissue that occurs when the force of a crash causes your brain to hit your skull. Like bruises elsewhere on your body, these injuries involve bleeding and swelling inside your brain, which can be life-threatening. Some car crash victims may experience confusion and coordination problems.

Skull Fracture

A skull fracture may occur if a violent car crash impact causes you to crack or shatter your skull. These breaks range from hairline cracks to deep fractures that expose brain tissue.

Coup-Contrecoup Injury

A coup-contrecoup injury is a serious type of traumatic brain injury (TBI) that involves damage at two sites in the brain. The coup is at the site of direct impact, while the opposite side of the brain is known as contrecoup. Symptoms vary depending on which areas of the brain are affected, but may include loss of consciousness, memory problems, nausea and vomiting.

Diffuse Axonal Injury

Car crash victims may sustain diffuse axonal injuries after sudden movement stretches and tears axons, nerve fibers, throughout the brain’s white matter.

Why Do Insurance Companies Fight Brain Injury Claims?

Insurance companies often challenge brain injury claims using tactics to help minimize payouts and protect company profits. Their goals do not align with yours, so they make low initial settlement offers to protect their interests. Other tactics they may try include delaying claim processing or extensively perusing victims' medical histories and social media in an attempt to find contradicting evidence. They frequently dispute causation, arguing symptoms existed before the accident or stem from other conditions. They may even question the severity of your brain injury, especially with mild TBIs where damage may not be visible on standard imaging tests. Insurance companies know brain injury claims can be expensive, potentially involving lifetime care costs, lost wages and reduced earning capacity. They also recognize that proving non-obvious symptoms like cognitive difficulties or personality changes can be challenging for victims. Therefore, it is vital to have solid evidence that links your injuries to the car accident.

What Medical Evidence Can Help to Support My Brain Injury Claim?

Strong medical evidence for brain injury claims includes:
  • Medical Records: Documents from the emergency room and hospital visits, treating physician notes, assessments and neurologist evaluations.
  • Diagnostic Tests: CT, MRI and PET scans can detect what type of TBI car crash victims have, along with EEGs.
  • Specialist Documentation: If car crash victims visit a specialist for their injuries, they can provide neuropsychological evaluations, cognitive function test results and speech or occupational therapy assessments.
  • Supporting Evidence: This type of evidence may include photos of visible injuries, witness statements about behavioral changes and work or school performance records showing decline.

Reasons Drivers Act Recklessly

Drivers engage in reckless behavior for psychological and situational reasons. Emotional states like rage, frustration or aggression often trigger dangerous driving choices. Some drivers feel invincible behind the wheel, causing them to speed, tailgate or weave through traffic without considering the consequences. Young or inexperienced drivers may lack proper risk assessment skills or feel peer pressure to drive dangerously. Some drivers disregard traffic laws, viewing them as inconvenient rather than essential safety measures. This combination of personal, emotional and situational factors creates dangerous conditions on heavily trafficked Charleston roads like I-26. Time pressure plays a significant role. Some drivers may be running late, causing them to rush to work or appointments, resulting in unnecessary risks. Other interruptions can lead to reckless drivers. Distraction from phones, passengers or other activities diverts attention from safe driving practices. Substances like alcohol and drugs can severely impair judgment and reaction time. If drivers take prescription drugs before they drive, it can also alter their behavior and become the root cause of their reckless driving.

What Are the Most Common Forms of Reckless Driving?

Reckless drivers have various types of behaviors and activities that they do. Some of the most common forms of reckless driving are:
  • Distracted Driving: This includes activities like texting, eating, adjusting your seat or review mirror while driving.
  • Speeding: Driving above the speed limit reduces reaction time and increases the risk of accidents.
  • Aggressive Driving: This involves tailgating, weaving through traffic or not yielding to other vehicles
  • Street Racing: Racing on public roads is hazardous and illegal
  • Disregarding Traffic Signs and Laws: Running red lights or not stopping at stop signs

How Does Reckless Driving Lead to an Accident?

Reckless driving creates dangerous situations that quickly escalate into crashes. Excessive speed reduces reaction time and increases impact force. When drivers weave through traffic or tailgate, they leave no safety margin for sudden stops or emergencies. Weather conditions and the flow of traffic could amplify these risks. During coastal storms or heavy tourism seasons, reckless driving becomes especially dangerous on routes like Highway 17 and the Ravenel Bridge. Roads already crowded with commuters, tourists and port traffic become hazardous when reckless drivers ignore safety protocols. In some incidents, reckless drivers can cause multiple-vehicle car accidents. Erratically changing lanes or running a red light can cause multiple vehicle accidents. These chain-reaction accidents frequently cause severe injuries and extensive property damage.

Are Reckless Drivers Always Liable for An Accident?

Reckless drivers typically bear primary liability for accidents, but other factors can influence fault. These drivers must generally prove another party's negligence contributed to the crash to reduce their liability. Contributing factors that may affect liability:
  • Road conditions or maintenance issues
  • Vehicle mechanical failures
  • Other drivers' reactions
  • Traffic signal malfunctions
In some cases, both parties may share fault for the car accident. This is called a modified comparative negligence system. In South Carolina, if both parties are found to be partially at fault, each party’s compensation will be reduced by their percentage of fault. For example, if you are found to be 30 percent at fault for an accident and your total settlement amount is $100,000, you will only receive $70,000. Note that a party cannot recover compensation if they are more than 50 percent at fault.

What Should I Do If I Encounter a Reckless Driver on The Road?

If you encounter a reckless driver, prioritize your safety by creating distance between your vehicle and theirs. Never engage with or challenge aggressive drivers. Key actions to take:
  • Pull over safely or change lanes to let them pass
  • Maintain a safe following distance
  • Call 911 to report dangerous driving
  • Note the vehicle description and license plate if safe
  • Exit the highway or take an alternate route if needed

Some drivers feel invincible behind the wheel, causing them to speed, tailgate or weave through traffic without considering the consequences. Young or inexperienced drivers may lack proper risk assessment skills or feel peer pressure to drive dangerously. Some drivers disregard traffic laws, viewing them as inconvenient rather than essential safety measures. This combination of personal, emotional and situational factors creates dangerous conditions on heavily trafficked Charleston roads like I-26. Time pressure plays a significant role. Some drivers may be running late, causing them to rush to work or appointments, resulting in unnecessary risks. Other interruptions can lead to reckless drivers. Distraction from phones, passengers or other activities diverts attention from safe driving practices. Substances like alcohol and drugs can severely impair judgment and reaction time. If drivers take prescription drugs before they drive, it can also alter their behavior and become the root cause of their reckless driving.

What Are the Most Common Forms of Reckless Driving?

Reckless drivers have various types of behaviors and activities that they do. Some of the most common forms of reckless driving are:
  • Distracted Driving: This includes activities like texting, eating, adjusting your seat or review mirror while driving.
  • Speeding: Driving above the speed limit reduces reaction time and increases the risk of accidents.
  • Aggressive Driving: This involves tailgating, weaving through traffic or not yielding to other vehicles
  • Street Racing: Racing on public roads is hazardous and illegal
  • Disregarding Traffic Signs and Laws: Running red lights or not stopping at stop signs

How Does Reckless Driving Lead to an Accident?

Reckless driving creates dangerous situations that quickly escalate into crashes. Excessive speed reduces reaction time and increases impact force. When drivers weave through traffic or tailgate, they leave no safety margin for sudden stops or emergencies. Weather conditions and the flow of traffic could amplify these risks. During coastal storms or heavy tourism seasons, reckless driving becomes especially dangerous on routes like Highway 17 and the Ravenel Bridge. Roads already crowded with commuters, tourists and port traffic become hazardous when reckless drivers ignore safety protocols. In some incidents, reckless drivers can cause multiple-vehicle car accidents. Erratically changing lanes or running a red light can cause multiple vehicle accidents. These chain-reaction accidents frequently cause severe injuries and extensive property damage.

Are Reckless Drivers Always Liable for An Accident?

Reckless drivers typically bear primary liability for accidents, but other factors can influence fault. These drivers must generally prove another party's negligence contributed to the crash to reduce their liability. Contributing factors that may affect liability:
  • Road conditions or maintenance issues
  • Vehicle mechanical failures
  • Other drivers' reactions
  • Traffic signal malfunctions
In some cases, both parties may share fault for the car accident. This is called a modified comparative negligence system. In South Carolina, if both parties are found to be partially at fault, each party’s compensation will be reduced by their percentage of fault. For example, if you are found to be 30 percent at fault for an accident and your total settlement amount is $100,000, you will only receive $70,000. Note that a party cannot recover compensation if they are more than 50 percent at fault.

What Should I Do If I Encounter a Reckless Driver on The Road?

If you encounter a reckless driver, prioritize your safety by creating distance between your vehicle and theirs. Never engage with or challenge aggressive drivers. Key actions to take:
  • Pull over safely or change lanes to let them pass
  • Maintain a safe following distance
  • Call 911 to report dangerous driving
  • Note the vehicle description and license plate if safe
  • Exit the highway or take an alternate route if needed

Visible scarring and disfigurement on a person's face can cause psychological harm, embarrassment and depression. It can also have a significant financial impact on both the victims and their families.

What Kinds of Facial Injuries Happen in Car Crashes?

A car accident can cause serious damage to facial bones, muscles, nerves and soft tissues. Below are some of the most common types of facial injuries caused by car crashes.

Soft Tissue Injuries

Cuts, bruises and burns across the face can result from broken glass or flying debris during a car accident. These injuries may range from minor scrapes to deep lacerations requiring plastic surgery. Even seemingly minor cuts on the face can leave permanent scars, affecting a victim's appearance and emotional well-being.

Facial Fractures

The face contains 14 different bones that can break during trauma. Common fractures include orbital fractures, which affect the eye socket, and cheekbone fractures, which are more likely to happen in side-impact collisions. Other types of fractures may include:
  • Nasal bone breaks from direct impacts
  • Cheekbone (zygomatic) fractures from side impacts
  • Jaw (mandible) fractures that affect eating and speaking
  • Upper jaw (maxilla) fractures requiring surgical repair

Dental Trauma

Dental trauma in a car accident typically happens when your head or mouth strikes an object or when the mouth abruptly closes due to the impact. For example, in a rear-end car accident, someone’s head or mouth can strike the steering wheel. Dental injuries during a car accident could be:
  • Broken or chipped teeth
  • Knocked-out teeth requiring immediate care
  • Fractured dental roots
  • Damaged gums and soft tissue
  • Jaw alignment problems affecting the victim's bite

Eye Injuries Trauma

Eye injuries from a car crash could leave victims with blurry vision or vision loss. Eye injuries may occur if the victim is struck in the face with a direct impact, such as from airbag deployment or shattered glass. Serious eye injuries may include:
  • Corneal scratches or tears
  • Orbital bone damage
  • Vision problems
  • Detached retina
  • Loss of eyesight

Nerve Damage

Facial injuries often involve some degree of nerve damage. The impact of a trauma may stretch, compress or even sever nerves. In a car accident, facial nerve damage happens when the impact forces the head or face against hard surfaces. Nerve damage may cause car crash victims to experience:
  • Loss of facial movement
  • Numbness or tingling
  • Problems with facial expressions
  • Difficulty eating or speaking
  • Chronic pain

Common Causes of Facial Scarring and Disfigurement

During a car crash, multiple factors can lead to facial scarring and disfigurement. The impact of a collision can be severe enough to thrust a victim's body and face against hard surfaces in the vehicle. Facial scarring and disfigurement may occur in a car crash as a result of:

Flying Glass and Debris

Shattered windshields and windows send sharp glass fragments flying through the vehicle at high speeds. These fragments can slice deep into facial tissue, causing severe lacerations that often result in permanent scarring. Side-impact collisions particularly increase the risk of glass-related facial injuries when windows explode inward.

Airbag Deployment Impact

While airbags save lives, their explosive deployment can cause serious facial injuries. The intense force and heat from deploying airbags can burn the skin, cause chemical burns or create facial abrasions. High-speed deployment may also drive debris into facial tissue.

Dashboard and Steering Wheel Impact

Sudden deceleration can throw drivers and passengers forward onto hard surfaces, like the dashboard or steering wheel. The resulting impact can break or crush facial bones and create wounds that cause permanent disfigurement.

Ejection Injuries

When victims get thrown from vehicles, their faces may hit window glass, metal from the vehicle or scrape across pavement. Road rash from sliding across asphalt can remove layers of facial skin. Additionally, impact with objects during ejection can shatter facial bones and create deep tissue damage.

Secondary Collision Damage

After the initial impact, loose objects inside the car become dangerous projectiles. Cell phones, water bottles and other items could strike the face. These secondary impacts often cause significant tissue damage and scarring.

Metal and Frame Intrusion

Sharp metal edges can penetrate the passenger compartment when a vehicle's frame collapses during impact. These twisted metal pieces can slice or puncture facial tissue, creating jagged wounds that are difficult to repair without visible scarring.

Burns and Chemical Exposure

Vehicle fires or chemical spills during crashes can cause severe facial burns. Thermal burns destroy tissue layers, while chemical burns from deployed airbags or leaking fluids can create permanent skin damage and discoloration.

How Much Compensation for Face Injury?

The amount of compensation you may receive for facial injury may vary depending on the factors and circumstances of your accident. However, insurance companies or courts may value your case depending on the expenses and damages you may incur.
  • Medical Expenses: Emergency room treatment, surgery costs, dental work, future medical needs, etc.
  • Lost Income and Earning Capacity: Facial injuries could mean you miss work, so you may receive compensation for loss of future earnings and loss of income due to recovery time.
  • Pain and Suffering: This compensation can cover physical pain from injuries, emotional trauma, depression and anxiety.

What Factors Impact My Compensation?

Different factors can impact your compensation. Some reasons why some cases may be valued at different costs may include:

Injury Severity and Permanence

The more severe and permanent your facial injuries, the higher your potential compensation. Insurance companies and courts will examine numerous elements such as depth and visibility of scarring, number of facial bones broken and extent of soft tissue damage.

Medical Documentation

Your medical documentation will serve as viable evidence for your legal case. Detailed emergency room records, surgery reports and photos can strengthen your case. Your attorney can also consult with medical experts to provide further clarity and testimony about the severity and extent of your injuries.

Liability and Fault

After a car crash, you must prove that the other party was at fault. It could affect your compensation if you are found to be partially at fault in a South Carolina car accident. For example, if you are 30 percent at fault and your compensation is $100,000, it will be reduced to $70,000.

Professional Impact

Facial injuries resulting from car accidents can significantly impact an individual's career. For example, if a car crash victim has a job that requires frequent public appearances or being in front of a camera, such injuries could affect their livelihood. This situation may lead to compensation covering reduced earning capacity or necessitate career changes due to disfigurement.

Quality of Life Changes

Courts and insurance companies may consider how facial injuries affect your daily life. If you experience life changes such as social anxiety, loss of enjoyment in activities or changes in personal relationships, be sure to provide evidence of these impacts. Some evidence you may use includes daily journals and records of canceled events or missed gatherings.

fBrake-checking causes some of Charleston's most hazardous traffic accidents. When a driver deliberately slams on their brakes, it creates chaos on busy roads.

  • What Is Brake Checking?
  • Why Drivers Brake Check and How It Endangers Motorists

  • Types of Evidence That Can Prove Brake Checking in Charleston
  • Steps to Take Immediately If You Are a Victim of Brake Checking
  • Call Roden Law After a Charleston Brake Checking Car Accident
If you have been involved in a brake-checking accident that caused your injuries and damages, it is vital you seek legal help after pursuing immediate medical care. Our Charleston car accident attorneys are here to help you throughout the legal process. Call our firm today to discuss your legal options and answer your questions. If we represent you, there are no upfront costs or fees to pay.

Schedule a free case review today: 1-844-RESULTS.

What Is Brake Checking?

Brake-checking is a dangerous driving behavior where a driver deliberately and suddenly applies their brakes when another vehicle is following closely behind. This action forces the following driver to brake abruptly or take risky actions to avoid a collision.

Why Drivers Brake Check and How It Endangers Motorists

Drivers may brake-check on highways when they feel someone is tailgating them. During road rage or aggression, drivers may feel pumped up to teach another driver a lesson, who they think is driving improperly. In high-traffic situations, drivers could get frustrated by another’s actions, especially if vehicles move slowly. Brake-checking can endanger drivers' safety because they can be in a hazardous car accident. In some cases, drivers can get involved in an altercation if brake-checking results from road rage.

How South Carolina’s 51 Percent Fault Rule Affects Brake-Checking Accidents

South Carolina operates on a modified comparative negligence law. This means you can still recover damages from a car crash as long as you are less than 50 percent at fault. The percentage of fault assessed against you directly determines your eligibility to recover compensation. Even a one percent difference can mean the difference between a partial recovery and no recovery at all. If you are 51 percent or greater at fault, you will not be able to recover compensation.

Types of Evidence That Can Prove Brake Checking in Charleston

If you were injured in a brake-checking crash, you will need compelling evidence to overcome the typical presumption that the tailing driver is always at fault for a rear-end crash. The most effective types of evidence that can establish a brake-checking claim includes:

Dashcam and Traffic Camera Footage

Video evidence provides the most definitive proof of brake checking. Dashcam footage showing a vehicle suddenly braking without apparent reason is powerful evidence in Charleston courts. Look for:
  • Clear views of the lead vehicle's brake lights activating suddenly
  • Absence of traffic or road hazards that would justify braking
  • Multiple braking episodes suggesting intentional behavior
  • The lead driver's actions before the brake-checking incident

Witness Testimony

Witnesses can provide testimony about a brake-checking incident. Charleston's busy roads often mean multiple drivers observe these dangerous maneuvers. Compelling witness testimony typically includes:
  • Observations of aggressive driving before the incident
  • Confirmation that no road hazards existed to justify sudden braking
  • Descriptions of multiple brake-checking attempts
  • Statements about the lead driver's behavior suggesting road rage

Electronic Vehicle Data

Various types of electronic data from the vehicles involved may provide additional evidence that support brake-checking claims in Charleston courts. Modern vehicles record extensive data that can be extracted after accidents:
  • Event Data Recorders (EDRs) capture sudden changes in speed, such as if the driver had to slam on the brakes
  • Braking patterns may show unusual or unnecessary braking
  • Speed data may reveal inconsistent driving behavior

Physical Evidence and Accident Reconstruction

An accident reconstructionist uses physical evidence from the scene, along with high tech tools to establish what happened. This type of evidence may include:
  • Skid mark patterns in the road, which indicates the driver had to brake suddenly
  • Impact analysis revealing the position and speeds of both vehicles
  • Damage patterns to involved vehicles that are consistent with sudden, unexpected braking
  • Road conditions that do not justify emergency stops

Steps to Take Immediately if You Are a Victim of Brake Checking

When another driver brake-checks you, act quickly to protect your safety and strengthen your legal claim. Pull over to a safe location if possible. After a collision, turn on your hazard lights and move to the shoulder or a nearby parking area, provided your vehicle is drivable. Stay in your car if getting out would endanger you, especially on highways and busy roads.

Call Law Enforcement

After a brake-checking car accident, call law enforcement to report the accident. When officers arrive, explain what happened without involving your emotions. Statements like “This driver made me mad” or “I am so annoyed” could be documented in a police report as a part of a police officer’s observation. A police officer can say you were upset or angry, which could misinterpret what happened during a car crash. Calmly describe the driver’s behavior before and during the brake check accident and remember to ask for a copy of the police report.

Document the Accident Scene

Document everything at the scene of the accident. Gather as much evidence as possible by taking photos of vehicles and license plates. Pictures of road conditions and weather can showcase what occurs during an accident.

Notify Your Insurance Company

Call your insurance company to inform them about the accident. Stick to essential information such as the accident's date, time and location. Avoid discussing fault until you have consulted with an attorney.

Call Roden Law After a Charleston Brake Checking Car Accident

Brake-checking accidents create complex liability situations that challenge standard fault assumptions. Attempting to navigate the legal process while you are recovering from your car accident injuries can take a toll on you. At Roden Law, we help you understand your legal options. If we determine you have a valid case and you choose us to represent you, we will negotiate with the insurance company and gather the evidence needed to strengthen your claim. You pay nothing for our legal services unless we win. Call us for a free consultation. We are here to answer your questions.

posts.before:
The sudden impact of a car crash can cause physical injuries that have life-altering changes. Hearing is one of your most vital senses, often overlooked in the aftermath of a car accident.

Table of Contents

  • How Car Accidents Cause Hearing Loss
  • What Type of Hearing Problems Victims Have After a Car Accident?
  • Proving Your Hearing Loss Is Link to the Accident
  • What Compensation I Can Recover for Accident Hearing Loss
  • Call Roden Law After Suffering from Hearing Loss in a Charleston Car Crash
If you notice ear injuries after a crash, seek medical attention immediately to begin your recovery. Once you have addressed your medical needs, it is highly recommended that you contact an attorney to pursue compensation for medical expenses and other damages. At Roden Law, our Charleston car accident attorneys can help you determine your legal options. During a free consultation, one of our attorneys will discuss your legal options with you and address any questions you may have. If we proceed with your potential case, you will not have to pay any upfront costs. Our firm only receives pay if we win your case.

Call today to request a free consultation: 1-844-RESULTS.

How Car Accidents Cause Hearing Loss

Car accidents can damage your hearing in several ways that some accident victims do not initially consider. Discovering how victims may damage their hearing during a car crash could help you gain more knowledge on the type of injuries that you have and how they may become severe.

Loud Noises and Trauma

The explosive sound of a collision can exceed 140 decibels, which is louder than a jet engine at takeoff. This intense noise can immediately damage the delicate hair cells in your inner ear that transmit sound signals to your brain. Even exposure to these extreme sound levels can cause permanent hearing damage or tinnitus (persistent ringing in the ears).

Airbag Deployment

Modern vehicles' lifesaving airbags deploy at speeds exceeding 200 mph, creating a shockwave and explosion that reaches 160 to 175 decibels. This sudden pressure change occurs inches from your ears, potentially causing:
  • Rupture of the eardrum (tympanic membrane)
  • Damage to the ossicles (tiny bones that transmit sound)
  • Acoustic trauma to inner ear structures

Head Trauma and TBI

The violent forces in a collision often cause your head to strike objects or the interior of the vehicle. These impacts can result in:
  • Temporal bone fractures affecting the ear canal
  • Labyrinthine concussion disrupting inner ear fluid
  • Traumatic brain injury affecting how your brain processes sound
  • Damage to auditory nerves carrying signals from ear to brain

Blood Flow Disruption

Neck injuries are common in car accidents and could temporarily or permanently alter blood flow to the inner ear, causing oxygen deprivation. Even brief interruptions to this blood supply can result in sudden loss of hearing.

Secondary Infections and Inflammation

Trauma to the ear region can create pathways for infection or trigger inflammatory responses that cause delayed hearing loss days or weeks after your accident. This delayed onset often leads victims to overlook the connection to their crash. Accident-related hearing damage often appears immediately but can also develop gradually in the days and weeks following your crash. This is why prompt medical evaluation is crucial after any collision, even if you initially feel fine.

What Type of Hearing Problems Victims Have After a Car Accident?

Due to the impact and forces involved in a car accident, victims are vulnerable to various types of injuries. Some of the injuries victims might experience could be:
  • Muffled Hearing: This may feel like listening underwater or having cotton in your ears. It can be caused by ear trauma, whiplash or a burst eardrum.
  • Tinnitus: Ringing, buzzing or hissing sounds in the ears, often following head or neck injuries.
  • Hearing Loss: This can be either temporary or permanent and is often caused by damage to the inner ear structures or auditory pathways.
  • Dizziness or Vertigo: These symptoms can indicate inner ear damage, affecting balance and hearing.
  • Ear Pain or Fullness: A sensation of pressure or fullness in the ears, which might suggest damage affecting hearing acuity
  • Conductive Hearing Loss: This occurs when sound waves cannot travel efficiently through the outer ear, ear canal, or middle ear to reach the inner ear.
  • Sensorineural Hearing Loss: SHL is caused by damage to the inner ear or the auditory nerve pathways. This typically occurs after loud noises or infections.
  • Mixed Hearing Loss: A combination of conductive and sensorineural hearing loss. This means there are issues in the outer or middle ear, the inner ear, or the auditory nerve.
  • Hyperacusis: A rare condition where sounds are perceived as unbearably loud and painful daily.

Proving Your Hearing Loss Is Link to the Accident

Establishing a clear connection between your car accident and hearing loss can help strengthen your case and increase your chances of receiving a claim. Insurance companies often challenge these claims, arguing that hearing problems existed before the crash or stem from other causes. Here is how to build a compelling case that proves your hearing damage resulted directly from the accident.
  • Seek Immediate Medical Attention: Visit an emergency room or your primary doctor as soon as you notice any changes to your hearing.
  • Specialized Medical Testing: Consult with a hearing specialist who can conduct evaluations, such as pure tone audiometry tests, speech recognition assessments and tympanometry.
  • Collect Documents of Pre-Accident Hearing Status: Previous hearing test results or medical records showing no prior complaints can debunk claims that your hearing loss predated the crash.
  • Connect Specific Accident Factors to Injuries: Work with your attorney to document details that could cause hearing damage, such as airbag deployment, window glass shatter or head impact against vehicle surfaces.
  • Testimony From Medical Experts: Hearing specialist doctors, such as audiologists and otolaryngologists, can provide expert testimony explaining the extent of your permanent hearing damage or how the crash caused it.
  • Consistent Medical Treatment: Maintain follow-up appointments and comply with recommended treatment to show the validity of your condition. It also creates an ongoing record of your hearing issues and their impact on your life.
  • Daily Impact Documentation: Keep a detailed journal describing how your hearing loss affects your daily activities, work performance, relationships and emotional well-being. This step can help quantify non-economic damages and reinforce the seriousness of your injuries.

What Compensation I Can Recover for Accident Hearing Loss

The type of compensation you can recover depends on the specific details of your case. However, hearing loss from a car accident can affect every aspect of your daily life. Below are some of the types of compensation you may be able to recover after suffering accident-related hearing damage:

Medical Expenses

You deserve full reimbursement for all hearing-related medical costs. Modern hearing aids typically cost between $3,000 and $7,000 per ear and need to be replaced every three to five years. These expenses can accumulate quickly, especially over a lifetime. Some related medical expenses for hearing loss after an accident may include:
  • Emergency room and hospital bills
  • Diagnostic tests and evaluations
  • Specialist consultations with audiologists and ENT physicians
  • Hearing aids and assistive listening devices
  • Medical device maintenance, batteries and replacements
  • Surgical interventions when applicable
  • Ongoing therapy and rehabilitation
  • Future medical care related to your hearing loss

Lost Income and Earning Capacity

Hearing loss can significantly impact your ability to work. For professionals in fields that require clear communication, such as education, customer service or healthcare, hearing damage can be career-ending, resulting in substantial lifetime earnings losses. Below are some of the ways that your income could be affected after a hearing loss due to an accident.
  • Wages lost during recovery and treatment
  • Reduced earnings if you cannot return to your previous position
  • Diminished future earning potential
  • Job retraining costs if your hearing loss prevents returning to your profession
  • Lost advancement opportunities
  • Early retirement considerations

Pain and Suffering

Non-economic damages compensate for the physical and emotional toll of hearing loss. These damages recognize that the inability to fully participate in conversations and enjoy sounds most people take for granted represents a significant loss to your quality of life.
  • Physical discomfort from tinnitus (constant ringing or buzzing)
  • Sleep disturbances caused by hearing damage
  • Mental anguish and emotional distress
  • Anxiety and depression related to communication difficulties
  • Loss of enjoyment in music, conversations and environmental sounds
  • Social isolation resulting from communication challenges

Call Roden Law After Suffering from Hearing Loss in a Charleston Car Crash

Living with hearing loss after a car accident creates daily challenges most people do not consider. Background noise in restaurants can make dining out frustrating, and the constant ringing in your ears may disrupt your sleep. These inconveniences and significant losses deserve fair compensation. At Roden Law, we have helped our clients secure millions of dollars in compensation. During a free consultation, we can determine if you have a valid case. There are no upfront costs or fees for any of our legal services.

Speak to one of our attorneys today: 1-844-RESULTS.

Why Drivers Have More Accidents Closer to Home and in Other Familiar Areas

Statistically, more crashes happen within five to 25 miles of where you live due to several key factors, including how we drive in familiar surroundings. Common reasons more collisions happen closer to home are because:

Drivers Are More Familiar With the Local Roads Near Their Home

Drivers can become complacent or "zone out" while driving on local roads they know well. When you drive the same routes repeatedly, your brain tends to shift into that "autopilot" state, but this is dangerous. Zoning out in that way impairs your ability to focus on the road, remain alert for potential hazards, and drive defensively.

Distraction

Distraction rates increase dramatically near homes. Since drivers are familiar with these routes, they are much more comfortable checking their phones, adjusting their music, or engaging with passengers. However, getting distracted, even on familiar roads, is dangerous. You could miss a pedestrian or pet darting into the road, or the vehicle in front of you braking at a stop sign or turning into the local convenience store without signaling. Getting distracted by your cellphone could even cause you to drift and crash into a utility pole, parked vehicle, or even someone's house.

The “Almost Home” Phenomenon

The "almost home" phenomenon affects many residents. After successfully navigating longer trips, drivers often relax their guard during the final minutes of their journey. This mental shift typically happens after drivers exit busy highways and enter residential neighborhoods. In some instances, drivers may fail to stop at stop signs or overlook pedestrians crossing the street.

Charleston Neighborhood Driving Hazards

Multiple neighborhoods present unique driving challenges that contribute to a high number of accidents near home.
  • Downtown Areas: Some of Charleston's downtown areas have narrow streets that could get congested with heavy traffic. This is likely to be the case if you are driving through downtown on the weekends or during the holidays.
  • Suburban Access Points: In some residential neighborhoods, there may be limited entry and exit roads, creating congestion hotspots. These bottlenecks become particularly hazardous during morning or evening rush hours when drivers are often distracted or fatigued.
  • Developing Areas: Charleston has multiple areas that are undergoing rapid development. New traffic patterns in familiar areas can catch drivers off guard, particularly where older neighborhood streets intersect with recently expanded main roads.
  • Mixed-Use Zones: Drivers regularly navigate areas where residential traffic mixes with commercial vehicles. This creates dangerous speed and size differentials even on streets that locals drive daily.
  • School Zone Congestion: The areas surrounding Charleston's schools pose unique hazards during drop-off and pick-up times. Parents familiar with these routes often multitask while driving, which increases the risk of accidents in areas with high pedestrian traffic.
  • Backing Out of Driveways: Exiting driveways onto residential streets can be dangerous if there is limited visibility, unexpected pedestrian and the false security of familiar surroundings.
  • Neighborhood Intersections Without Signals: Intersections that do not have signals in residential areas account for a significant proportion of crashes near homes. Drivers may unintentionally ignore familiar stop signs or fail to yield at intersections they navigate daily.
  • Shopping Center Parking Lots: Minor collisions are likely to happen in neighborhood shopping areas. The combination of pedestrians, cart returns and multiple vehicles maneuvering in tight spaces creates conditions for fender-benders.

How Weather and Road Conditions Affect Local Accidents

Charleston's unique environment creates specific weather and road challenges that contribute to close-to-home accidents:

Flash Flooding on Familiar Routes

Charleston's low elevation makes residential streets highly susceptible to rapid flooding, even during moderate rainfall. Residents often underestimate water depth on familiar roads, particularly in flood-prone neighborhoods.

Sudden Coastal Fog Patterns

Morning fog develops quickly along Charleston's waterways and can dramatically reduce visibility on residential streets near harbors or rivers. Locals driving familiar routes often maintain unsafe speeds despite adverse weather conditions.

Hurricane Season Road Debris

Debris left behind by a hurricane can lead to an accident. Residents may have to swerve unexpectedly to avoid fallen branches or flood-related road damage.

Tourist Season Traffic Pattern Changes

Seasonal tourism alters traffic patterns throughout Charleston's residential areas as visitors seek shortcuts to avoid congestion. Locals often do not expect familiar streets to get so busy during peak tourist season.

What To Do After a Neighborhood Accident in Charleston

Even if you are in a car accident in your neighborhood, it is still essential to take steps to protect your health and legal rights.

Stay Safe

Ensure your safety first by moving your vehicle out of traffic. If possible, check all parties for injuries. Even in minor neighborhood crashes, activate hazard lights so drivers can stop or slow down if they drive near your vehicle. This helps prevent further collisions, especially in heavy traffic, low visibility, or high-speed areas. Visit a doctor even if you feel fine initially. A diagnostic test or examination can reveal the full extent of your injuries so that you can get the medical treatment you need to recover.

Report the accident to the police by calling 9-1-1. Some individuals may hesitate to call the police for minor accidents that occur near their homes. However, reporting the accident can help your insurance claims and could provide vital evidence that can strengthen your case.

Collect Evidence

If possible, take photos of the vehicle damage, street conditions, and the overall accident location. Pay special attention to any neighborhood-specific factors, such as unmarked dips, faded stop signs, or overgrown vegetation, that may have contributed to the collision. posts.before:
Unlike traditional intersections with clear right-of-way rules, roundabouts operate under a unique set of traffic expectations. Many drivers do not fully understand the right of way rules in a roundabout, which could lead to crashes due to driver confusion, error or negligence.

Table of Contents

  • What Are the Most Frequent Causes of Roundabout Crashes?
  • Common Types of Roundabout Accidents in Charleston
  • Who Is At Fault in Charleston Roundabout Crashes?
  • Challenges of Proving Fault in Charleston Roundabout Accidents
  • Need Legal Help? Call Roden Law After a Roundabout Car Accident.
At Roden Law, our firm is dedicated to helping crash victims recover the compensation they need after being injured by another driver's negligence.  If you have been in a roundabout car accident, our experienced Charleston car accident lawyers are prepared to discuss your situation, answer your questions and discuss your potential legal options.

Call our Charleston lawyers today for a free case review: 1-844-RESULTS.

What Are the Most Frequent Causes of Roundabout Crashes?

Roundabouts create unique traffic challenges that lead to several predictable accident patterns. These crashes typically occur due to specific driver behaviors and design issues:

Failure to Yield When Entering Roundabouts

One common way roundabout accidents occur is when drivers entering the circle mistakenly believe they have the right-of-way and fail to yield to vehicles already driving in the circle. This failure to yield can cause serious side-impact collisions with other drivers in the circle.

Excessive Speed

Vehicles entering or circulating too quickly reduce reaction time and increase crash severity. The curved design of roundabouts requires appropriate speed adjustment, which many drivers fail to make.

Improper Lane Changes

In multi-lane roundabouts, drivers frequently change lanes improperly or exit from the wrong lane. This creates dangerous accidents when vehicles unexpectedly cross paths.

Unexpected Stops

Drivers in roundabouts may make sudden stops due to hesitation at entry points, which could lead to rear-end crashes. If a driver follows another vehicle too closely or brakes unexpectedly, rear-end car crashes are likely.

Poor Visibility Conditions

Charleston's frequent coastal fog and heavy rainfall reduces visibility, making it difficult to correctly assess traffic when entering roundabouts.

Distracted Driving

Using phones, adjusting GPS systems, or other distractions while approaching roundabouts prevents drivers from adequately assessing the complex traffic environment.

Improper Signaling

Many drivers fail to signal when exiting the roundabout, leaving others guessing their intentions and creating collision risks when other vehicles attempt to enter.

Common Types of Roundabout Accidents in Charleston

Car accidents in roundabouts could create several distinct accident patterns that could lead to the following types of car accidents:

Entry Point Collisions

The most frequent crashes occur when vehicles enter the roundabout without yielding to circulating traffic. This could create T-bone or side-impact collisions. The lack of visibility at entry points of roundabouts may lead to an accident.

Rear-End Accidents

Sudden stops at roundabout entry points cause numerous rear-end collisions, especially during tourist season when unfamiliar drivers hesitate unexpectedly. Seasonal traffic during summer months could increase near tourist areas.

Exit Point Sideswipes

When drivers fail to signal their exit intentions, other vehicles attempting to enter often misjudge timing and cause sideswipe collisions. This pattern is typical during rush hour periods.

Cyclist and Pedestrian Incidents

Charleston's bicyclists are vulnerable to roundabout car accidents, especially when drivers fail to take reasonable measures to check for cyclists. Cyclists may also share some liability if they do not follow the state's bicycle laws and incorrectly position themselves within the flow of traffic.

Low-Speed Merging Accidents

Even at reduced speed, vehicles could collide when trying to merge into tight spaces in congested roundabouts. Drivers often become complacent in low-speed environments, paying less attention to proper yielding and signaling because they assume the reduced speed makes reactions less critical. Also, lower speed can encourage impatient drivers to attempt risky entries into small gaps, particularly during rush hour.

Who Is At Fault in Charleston Roundabout Crashes?

Fault for Charleston roundabout accidents is based on which driver broke any right-of-way rules or traffic laws.  A few key principles help decide who is responsible:

Drivers Entering Roundabouts

Drivers entering the roundabout are most likely to become responsible for an accident. South Carolina law requires entering vehicles to yield to traffic already circulating. Drivers who enter without yielding bear primary fault when collisions occur.

Multiple Vehicles

When multiple vehicles are involved, liability often spreads across drivers based on the percentage of fault. For instance, if a driver stops unexpectedly within the roundabout, causing a chain reaction, that driver may share fault with others who followed too closely.

Government Entities May Share Liability

In some cases, Charleston County or SCDOT may bear partial responsibility for roundabout crashes if the following occurred.
  • Inadequate signage
  • Poor visibility due to landscaping
  • Improper design or maintenance
  • Confusing lane markings

Commercial Truck Drivers and Companies

When commercial vehicles are involved in roundabout accidents, the driver and their employer may share liability, particularly if the company fails to provide proper training on navigating these intersections. Truck accidents have a different dynamic compared to regular car accidents. Because trucks carry heavy loads, collisions with smaller vehicles can cause severe blunt force impacts. As a result, this could lead to more severe damages and injuries.

Challenges of Proving Fault in Charleston Roundabout Accidents

Roundabout crashes create unique evidence challenges that make proving who is at fault difficult. Car crash victims may face the following obstacles, especially if they do not have legal representation or do not know how to navigate the legal process.

Conflicting Driver Accounts

Without clear traffic signals or stop signs, drivers often provide contradictory events. Each party may believe they had the right of way. This creates a “your word against mine” scenario that insurance companies exploit to minimize payouts.

Limited Witness Availability

The circular flow of roundabouts means witnesses often continue moving and leave the scene, unaware an accident occurred behind them. This results in fewer independent observers compared to traditional intersection crashes.

Inadequate Police Documentation

Police reports frequently lack detailed, roundabout-specific information. Officers may not document vital details necessary to determine fault, like entry points or lane positions.

Limited Camera Coverage

While downtown Charleston has traffic cameras at major intersections, many suburban roundabouts lack video surveillance, eliminating objective evidence that could establish fault.

Rapidly Changing Evidence

The high-traffic nature of Charleston's roundabouts means physical evidence like skid marks and vehicle debris quickly erode before proper documentation occurs. These challenges highlight the importance of immediate investigation and legal representation after a car accident to preserve evidence and establish liability.

Need Legal Help? Call Roden Law After a Roundabout Car Accident.

Roundabout car accidents can create significant challenges in determining fault. Victims will need solid evidence to secure fair compensation for their injuries, vehicle damage, and other losses. You do not have to go through the legal process alone. At Roden Law, you pay no upfront costs or out-of-pocket fees to engage our services. Experienced Lawyers. Proven Results: 1-844-RESULTS

The pressure to return to work after a car crash is overwhelming, especially when you have significant injuries. Medical bills can pile up while your income disappears, creating a financial burden for you and your family.

If you are worried about returning to work and not sure how to seek compensation, a trusted licensed attorney can help you determine your legal options. Find out if you have a valid claim by speaking to a lawyer about the details of your incident. At Roden Law, our Charleston car accident lawyers are here to help you throughout the legal process. If you have a valid case, our firm can negotiate with the insurance company and gather evidence that links your injuries to the accident.

Request a free consultation with our attorneys: 1-844-RESULTS

How Soon Is Too Soon To Return to Work After a Car Accident in Charleston?

There is no set time to return to work after a car accident. The appropriate time depends on your specific injuries, job requirements, and your doctor’s recommendations. You need to take into consideration the following to identify when the right time is to return to work.

Follow Your Doctor’s Recommendations

Your doctor’s professional recommendations are based on their knowledge, your specific injuries, and recovery progress. When you ignore this medical recommendation, you risk your health and weaken your injury claim.

Consider Your Physical Demands

The type of occupation you have can significantly impact the decision to return to work. For example, office workers with stationary duties may most likely go to work sooner than construction workers, hospitality staff, or healthcare providers whose jobs require physical exertion.

Who Decides When I Am Ready to Return to Work After a Car Crash?

Several key parties influence the decision about when you are ready to return to work after an accident. Each individual or party plays a distinct role in this decision:

Your Medical Providers

Your treating physicians hold the primary responsibility in determining when you are medically cleared to go back to work activities. These healthcare professionals base their decisions on:
  • Objective medical findings from exams, imaging, and tests
  • Your reported pain levels and functional limitations
  • Progress in physical therapy or other treatments
  • Specific physical requirements of your job duties

Your Employer

While your doctor determines medical clearance, your employer makes decisions about accommodating any restrictions or limitations. Some workplaces may offer flexible arrangements like:
  • Modified or light-duty assignments
  • Reduced hours or altered schedules
  • Temporary reassignment to less physically demanding roles
  • Work-from-home options during recovery
South Carolina employers are not legally required to hold your position, but many have return-to-work policies designed to help injured employees’ transition back safely. Review your company’s policies to plan your return to work.

Your Insurance Provider

Those who have short-term disability coverage may have insurance providers influence their return-to-work timing by determining benefit eligibility periods. These insurers typically:
  • Require regular medical documentation of continued disability
  • May conduct independent medical examinations
  • Often have case managers who coordinate with your doctors
  • Set specific benefit duration limits based on your policy
Workers’ compensation insurers play a particularly active role if your accident occurred during work hours, potentially requiring their own medical evaluations before approving your return.

Your Final Decision

Although various parties provide guidance and requirements, ultimately you make the final decision about returning to work. Your personal assessment of how ready you are to return to work matters, especially when:
  • You experience symptoms or limitations your doctor may not fully recognized
  • Your workplace presents unique challenges not addressed in generic restrictions
  • Financial pressures create urgency not reflected in medical recommendations

What Happens If I Can Not Afford to Miss Work After My Car Crash?

If you cannot afford to miss work after a car crash, you have other options that you can explore. You can look at your insurance coverage. Personal Injury Protection (PIP) may cover up to 80 percent of lost wages if you have no-fault coverage. Also, at-fault driver’s insurance can compensate for lost wages through a personal injury claim. You can discuss with your employers about remote work possibilities or modified duties. Most employers offer paid time off or sick leave which can be used during your recovery time. Depending on the medical conditions, some individuals may use the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) protection. Those who are eligible can have up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job protected leave per year for certain family and medical reasons. While you are on unpaid leave, employees are guaranteed their job or an equivalent position when they return.

How Do My Doctor's Work Restrictions Impact My Charleston Car Accident Claim?

When you are injured in a car accident, your doctor’s work restriction can significantly have an impact on your compensation claim.
  • Medical Evidence Value: Doctor testimony serves as crucial evidence in your case, establishing causation between the accident and your injuries.
  • Lost Wages: Work restrictions directly affect wage compensation, especially if you cannot return to your profession or earn at the same level.
  • Future Expenses: Your claim should include medical expenses if you need long-term care due to permanent impairments.
  • Permanent Restrictions: Work restrictions provide powerful evidence of disability. For example, a “no lifting over 15 pounds” restriction might significantly impact construction workers.
  • Maximum Medical Improvement: Your doctor determines when you have reached maximum medical improvement, establishing whether you will have permanent restrictions affecting your claim value.

What If My Employer Pressures Me to Return to Work After My Accident?

Pressure to return to work after a car accident can create significant stress during an already difficult recovery period. You will need to handle this circumstance by considering your employer pressure, protecting your health, and legal rights. Even if your employer or insurance company pressures you to return to work, only a medical professional is qualified to determine when you can safely return. Your doctor will base this decision on your specific injuries and recovery progress. Under no circumstances should you feel required to return to work before receiving your doctor's clearance. Your doctor might choose to wait until you make a complete recovery or might release you with certain restrictions.

How Insurance Adjusters Monitor Your Return to Work After an Accident

Insurance adjusters evaluate claims to determine liability. However, their primary goal is to minimize payouts by investigating incidents and gathering evidence that could reduce compensation. Some of the surveillance methods that insurance adjusters may use to observe victims are:
  • Physical Monitoring: Insurance companies may hire private investigators to follow claimants in public or observe them outside their homes to verify claims.
  • Social Media Tracking: Adjusters routinely monitor social media profiles for photos, videos, or posts suggesting you are more active than your claim indicates.
  • Workplace Observation: Adjusters may increase monitoring if they notice inconsistencies between your reported injuries and observed activities, especially when you return to work.

Can Working Through Pain Reduce My Charleston Car Accident Settlement?

You can potentially reduce your settlement amount if you decide to work through pain. Insurance companies look at the severity and impact of your injuries when deciding on the amount of compensation. If you continue to work despite your pain, the insurance company could perceive that your injuries are not as severe, which could lead to a lower settlement. If you ignore your doctor’s advice and later try to claim damages for related issues, your payout may be reduced, especially if most people would have followed that advice.

What If My Employer Offers Me Light Duties or a Shorter Work Day?

If your employer offers you light duty work, understand what it means. Ask your employer what type of modified or alternative roles will be adjusted. You should know if it is less physically demanding and need to consider your current health limitations while you recover from an injury. Here are some other things you want to take before accepting light duty or shorter work days.
  • Consult your doctor and provide your employer with your doctor's note outlining your condition and recommended recovery plan.
  • Employers are not required to offer light duty. If they do not, they typically pay temporary disability benefits through workers' compensation
  • Your employer cannot penalize you for using workers' compensation benefits and must allow you to return to your original job once you have fully recovered.
  • Gradually start with part-time hours or specific days to ease back into responsibilities while reducing the risk of reinjury.

How Roden Law Protects Charleston Clients Who Need to Return to Work

Prematurely returning to work after a car accident can significantly impact your injury claim. You do not have to work through your crash pain, receive the medical attention that you need and seek legal representation to pursue a fair compensation. At Roden Law, we understand the complex matters that victims face while managing their recovery, employment obligations, and pursuit of fair compensation. Our knowledgeable attorneys can provide the guidance needed to navigate these difficult decisions, ensuring that your health and legal rights are protected throughout the claims process.
